Summary

The picks and why

Jamf Pro TIER 1

Two layers. Tenant hardening through the Jamf Pro API, mapped to the DISA Jamf Pro EMM STIG V3R2 (29 rules). Fleet compliance through Jamf's Compliance Benchmarks API (Beta, macOS only), keyed on NIST mSCP rule IDs, which are CC BY 4.0.

Okta TIER 1

DISA Okta IDaaS STIG V1R3: 29 rules, all readable through the Okta Management API, public domain and co-developed with Okta. CIS publishes no Okta benchmark and CISA SCuBA has no Okta baseline. Small effort.

Gaps in core Maester CORE

CIS Intune for Apple, Android and Windows; Microsoft's Intune security baselines; CISA SCuBA Power Platform and Power BI (missing from cisa-scuba.json); the DISA Entra ID STIG. None needs a new connector.

Google Workspace, grown TIER 1

Already in flight. Add CIS Chrome Browser Cloud Management v1.0.0 and CIS ChromeOS v1.2.0 through the Chrome Policy API, using the same Google connection.

Infrastructure next to M365

CIS Azure Foundations 7.0.0 reuses the Azure connection. VMware vSphere works natively through PowerCLI and is underserved. Hybrid Exchange can wrap Microsoft's MIT-licensed HealthChecker.

MSP wins

Sophos Central's Account Health Check API returns vendor-scored posture as JSON (small effort). Veeam's Security & Compliance Analyzer is reachable from PowerShell.

Framework-only packs TIER 3

Close to free: catalogues plus Control mappings onto existing tests. NIST 800-53 r5 from OSCAL, 800-171/CMMC, CSF 2.0, CIS Controls v8.1, CISA CPG 2.0, Canada GC Guardrails, DISA AD STIGs, ISO 27001 Annex A IDs.

One tool to wrap

Prowler (Apache-2.0) covers AWS, GCP, Oracle Cloud, Kubernetes, Cloudflare, Okta and more. Import its results rather than rebuilding AWS or GCP CIS checks in Maester.

TIER 1

Build next

  1. Jamf Pro. The named interest, with a formal anchor in mSCP, CIS and DISA. Ship tenant checks first; fleet checks depend on a Beta API. See Jamf in detail.
  2. Okta (DISA Okta IDaaS STIG V1R3).
    • 29 rules (3 High, 26 Medium): V-273186 to V-273209 plus V-279689 to V-279693 for API tokens and network zones.
    • Rules cover session idle and lifetime, Admin Console and Dashboard MFA, phishing-resistant authenticators, password policy, lockout, 35-day inactivity, log offload, API tokens restricted by network zone, and blocking anonymisers.
    • Use an OAuth service app with private-key JWT and read-only scopes. The official Okta.PowerShell module documents only device-auth and SSWS tokens, so call the API with Invoke-RestMethod and handle the JWT yourself.
    • Make DoD-only rules (PIV, DoW-approved CAs, FIPS Okta Verify) optional.
    • Okta's Feb 2026 blog calls V1R2 "1.1"; record that in the catalogue. Prowler's mapping is still V1R2.
  3. Intune for Apple CORE
    • CIS publishes an Intune-specific benchmark for each OS release. CIS IDs change between editions, so keep one framework file per edition (e.g. cis-intune-macos-26).
    • The main work is mapping Settings Catalog definition IDs to CIS recommendations, and handling assignments and conflicts.
    • Put the 3-rule DISA Intune MDM Service STIG (V1R2, 1 Jul 2026) in core Intune checks.
  4. Intune security baselines CORE
    • For each baseline type, check that a profile on the latest version exists and is assigned broadly, none is stuck on an old version, and no setting is weakened against the template default.
    • Defaults come from Graph at runtime, so there is no value table to maintain.
    • This builds the effective-settings resolver that CIS Intune for Windows (large effort) needs later.
  5. Power Platform and Power BI SCuBA CORE
    • tests/cisa/frameworks/cisa-scuba.json holds only MS.AAD, MS.EXO, MS.SECURITYSUITE and MS.SHAREPOINT (confirmed in the repo).
    • Check that Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell works on PowerShell 7 before relying on it unverified; calling the REST APIs directly may be safer.
  6. Google Workspace extensions. Add the CIS GWS catalogue (IDs, Level, Profile) and map each native test to both cis-gws and the SCuBA GWS IDs. ScubaGoggles v1.1.0's OSCAL catalogue can seed the SCuBA file. Add Chrome CBCM and ChromeOS checks; the read-only Chrome Policy scope name is unverified.
  7. CIS Azure Foundations 7.0.0. Native ARM and Resource Graph checks. Identity sections overlap CIS M365 and Entra checks, so make those shims. Defender for Cloud MCSB/CIS results can be imported optionally.
  8. Exchange Server (hybrid). Wrap HealthChecker (MIT), which writes per-server XML, HTML and a JSON vulnerability report. Add native Exchange Management Shell checks mapped to CIS Exchange 2019 v1.0.1 and the DISA Exchange 2019 STIGs. CIS has no Exchange SE benchmark, so map SE servers to the 2019 controls.
  9. Sophos Central Health Check. GET api-<region>.central.sophos.com/account-health-check/v1/health-check with the X-Tenant-ID header. Categories: protection, policy, exclusions, tamperProtection, plus firewall backup. The Partner API reaches many tenants with one connector.

What the pack would check

Layer 1 · Tenant hardening

Jamf Pro API (Modern /api and Classic /JSSResource), OAuth2 client credentials bound to a read-only API Role. Maester-authored checks, plus Jamf Pro EMM STIG references where a rule applies.

  • SSO enforced; local login limited to break-glass accounts
  • API clients and roles: least privilege, no stale clients, no wildcard privileges
  • Number of full-access admins; account and group hygiene
  • Console password and lockout policy
  • Supported Jamf Pro version
  • Automated Device Enrolment used; user-initiated enrolment restricted
  • FileVault, Gatekeeper and SIP profiles scoped to all computers
  • FileVault recovery-key escrow
  • Supported macOS versions across the fleet; stale check-ins
Layer 2 · Fleet compliance

Jamf Compliance Benchmarks API: https://{region}.api.jamfcloud.com/compliance-benchmarks, scope compliance-benchmarks:read, X-Environment-Id header.

  • One result per mSCP rule: % of devices passing against a threshold, with CIS macOS and STIG IDs in Control
  • Labelled Beta; needs Jamf Pro 11.16+ with Jamf Account SSO
  • Not on-prem, Premium Cloud Plus or StateRAMP; macOS only (iOS on the roadmap)
  • Confirmed baselines: CIS L1/L2, NIST 800-53r5 L/M/H. STIG and CMMC announced, not confirmed
  • Fallback: mSCP <baseline>_compliance.sh writes results to an extension attribute Maester reads through inventory
Optional modules
  • Jamf Protect (GraphQL on the same Platform gateway): plans assigned to all Macs, prevention mode, definitions current, audit logging. Compliance/Insights data is not in the API.
  • Apple Business Manager: every org device assigned to an MDM server, no stale MDM servers.
  • jamf-cli (Jamf-Concepts, MIT, Go) covers Pro, Classic, Protect, School and Compliance Benchmarks with JSON output; useful for endpoint discovery or to wrap.

Design notes

  • Key the framework catalogue by mSCP rule ID. CC BY 4.0 allows this with attribution; never include Apple's vendor description text.
  • CIS macOS IDs change between editions, so carry them as cross-references rather than primary keys.
  • A pack shipped with Maester lives in packs/<name>/ with its own code; a community pack follows the one-repo-per-pack model used for ScubaGear and ScubaGoggles.

Licensing

What a pack may ship

  • CIS benchmarks. PDFs are free for non-commercial use with registration. XCCDF, Build Kits and CIS-CAT content are for SecureSuite members only. Framework files may hold only IDs and facts such as Level and Profile, never benchmark text, and test guides must not paraphrase it closely. Some benchmarks, such as CIS VMware ESXi, are members-only altogether. Verify the CIS Controls v8.1 licence before shipping safeguard IDs and IG tags.
  • DISA STIGs. US Government work in the public domain, distributed as XCCDF; rule text may be shown. Cite public.cyber.mil rather than mirrors. Make DoD-specific rules (DoW banner, PIV, DoW CAs, FIPS devices) optional or parameters.
  • CISA SCuBA baselines (ScubaGear, ScubaGoggles) are CC0.
  • mSCP is CC BY 4.0: attribution required, Apple "Vendor Description" text excluded.
  • NIST publications and OSCAL content are public domain. BSI Grundschutz++ is CC BY-SA 4.0, so keep derived files separate. CSA CCM and SSCF need registration with unclear redistribution terms. ISO 27001 is paid (IDs and short names only). PCI DSS comes under a licence agreement. AICPA TSC is copyrighted.
  • Vendor guidance (Microsoft, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Broadcom SCG, Sophos, Tailscale) can be referenced by setting name; check terms before copying text or spreadsheets.
  • Tool licences that limit reuse: Fleet EE (CIS policies), PingCastle (no paid service without a commercial licence), Databricks License, and GPL tools.

where do we get jamf and okta tests from?

Neither product has a ready-made set of tests to copy. In both cases the requirements come from a published standard, and we write each check ourselves against the product's API.

## Okta

**The requirements come from DISA's Okta IDaaS STIG (V1R3, 30 Sep 2026, 29 rules).**
- It's public domain. You download it as XCCDF (XML) from public.cyber.mil, or read it on the cyber.trackr.live mirror.
- Each rule has a rule ID (V-273186…), a severity, **check text** (what to look at in the Okta admin console) and **fix text**.
- Each test turns one rule's check text into an Okta Management API call. For example, `GET /api/v1/policies?type=OKTA_SIGN_ON` covers the session idle and lifetime rules.
- The XCCDF can generate the framework file (rule IDs, severity) automatically. That's the same pattern as `build/asd/Update-AsdFramework.ps1`.

**Reference implementations:**
- **Prowler** (Apache-2.0) already implements the Okta STIG, though only V1R2. Its checks show which API endpoint and field each rule needs. The licence allows reusing them with attribution.
- **okta-inspector-py** is GPL-3.0. Read it for ideas, but don't copy its code.

**Gaps:** a few rules are DoD-only (PIV cards, DoD certificate authorities, FIPS Okta Verify). Make those optional parameters for commercial tenants.

## Jamf

Jamf's checks come from two different places:

**1. The Jamf Pro tenant itself: SSO, API roles, admin accounts, lockout, version.**
- DISA's Jamf Pro v10.x EMM STIG (V3R2, 29 rules) gives a public-domain starting point. It's dated: still titled v10.x and scoped to iOS management.
- Most of these tests would be **Maester-authored**, the same way the MT.xxxx checks are, using the Jamf Pro API (e.g. `GET /v3/sso`, API roles, accounts).
- No benchmark exists for most tenant hygiene: stale API clients, too many full admins, FileVault key escrow. So we'd be writing the standard as well as the tests.

**2. Mac fleet compliance: is each Mac meeting CIS or NIST?**
- **NIST's macOS Security Compliance Project** (github.com/usnistgov/macos_security, CC BY 4.0) is the source. Its `rules/` folder has one YAML file per rule. Each file holds the rule ID, the shell check, the expected result, the fix, and cross-references to CIS macOS, the DISA STIG and 800-53. That gives us the framework catalogue directly.
- The rules run on each Mac, not remotely, so Maester reads the results rather than running the checks:
  - **Jamf's Compliance Benchmarks API** returns the pass rate per mSCP rule. That's one Maester test per rule, passing above a threshold. Limits: Beta, cloud only, Jamf Pro 11.16+, macOS only.
  - **Fallback:** the customer deploys mSCP's compliance script, which writes results into a Jamf extension attribute that Maester reads through the inventory API.

So for Okta the work is mostly translation: 29 STIG rules into 29 API checks, with Prowler as a crib sheet. Jamf is more original work for the tenant layer. The fleet layer is mostly mapping mSCP rule IDs to the results Jamf already reports.

# Maester Packs index

The site and index behind [packs.maester.cloud](https://packs.maester.cloud): the list of Maester Packs, a page per pack
with its tests, connector and security scan, the `index.json`, `codes.json` and `blocklist.json` that
`Find-MtPack` and Maester read, and `catalog.json`, every listed pack with its tests, which maester.dev's test catalog
reads. The design is section 7 and 8 of the Maester Packs design (maester365/maester#2396).

```
data/       sources.json (extra repositories to index); seed/ holds the starting reserved codes, blocklist, official and
            featured lists, which `npm run db:seed` copies into D1. After that, admins manage them on /admin
            sample/ is a built index of the packs in fixtures/, so the site builds and CI runs without the network
indexer/    Invoke-PackIndex.ps1: fetches, validates and scans every pack with Maester's own checks
site/       the static site (Astro), built from the index
worker/     the Cloudflare Worker: install events, Maester's run telemetry, usage counts and the scan queue, at /api/v1/*
```

## How a pack gets listed

1. Someone runs `Install-MtPack owner/repo`. Maester posts an install event to `/api/v1/events`, which queues the
   repository. Its status page then says what is needed to list it.
2. Every ten minutes the **Index** workflow's `scan` job reads the queue, downloads each pack at its latest release
   and runs Maester's `Test-MtPackContent` on it. Nothing in a pack runs. The job has no secrets and a read-only token.
3. The index applies its own rules: the repository must be public (private and internal ones are never listed), the
   pack must be published on the site (below), the blocklist, a 30-day minimum owner account age, duplicate content
   and a tagged release.
4. The `publish` job writes the result to the `listings` branch, builds the site, bundles both Workers and writes them
   to the `deploy` branch, which Cloudflare deploys (see Deploying below).

**The pack registry.** A pack is listed only after an admin of its repository signs in at /account and presses
Publish. The Worker checks the repository is public and registers the manifest's `Guid` and `Code` to the repository's
owner (by GitHub ID). From then on the Guid keeps that code and owner for good, and nobody else can publish that code,
even if the repository is made private or deleted. A release that changes the code for a registered Guid is not listed
(`CodeChanged`): the publisher goes back, or gives the pack a new Guid. A release of a published pack that changes
its Guid but keeps its code is not listed either (`GuidChanged`): the publisher sets the Guid back. A copied manifest
is refused (`GuidTaken`), as is a registered or reserved code (`CodeTaken`). Only an admin can remove a registration, on /admin.

**Hiding a pack.** An admin of a pack's repository can hide it from the site for a while, on /account (My Packs),
and show it again there. The next index run leaves it out (`Hidden`) and its status page says why. Its Guid and code
stay registered to it, and Maester still installs it from its repository: hiding only takes it off the site.

---
title: Writing a pack
description: Create, check and publish a Maester Pack, with its manifest, tests, helpers and connector.
sidebar:

# Writing a pack

:::tip[Guided setup]
To make a pack without writing the files by hand, use the guided setup at
[packs.maester.cloud/publish](https://packs.maester.cloud/publish). It copies the
[demo pack](https://github.com/maester365/maester-pack-demo) into a repository of yours, or starts from an empty one,
and fills in the manifest, the pack's Guide, its tests and its banner from a form. Then it releases the pack and
publishes it. It writes the same files this page describes, so you can change any of them later by hand.
:::

A pack is a folder with a `maester-pack.json`. Create one with `New-MtPack`:

```powershell
New-MtPack -Path ./maester-google-workspace -Id contoso.google-workspace -Code CNT -Connector
Test-MtPack ./maester-google-workspace
Invoke-MtTest -Path ./maester-google-workspace
```

`Invoke-MtTest -Path` runs the pack from its folder, with its helpers and connector, and reloads it on every call.
`Test-MtPack` runs every check `Install-MtPack` runs, without installing: use it in the pack's own CI.

```text
maester-google-workspace/
  maester-pack.json
  README.md
  tests/
    suite.json
    Test.MP.CNT.1001.ps1
    Test.MP.CNT.1001.md
  helpers/
    Get-CntWorkspaceSetting.ps1
  connector/
    Connect-CntGoogleWorkspace.ps1
```

To share the pack, push the folder to a GitHub repository owned by the publisher and create a release. A release made
[immutable](https://docs.github.com/repositories/releasing-projects-on-github/about-releases) starts its
cooldown when it is published; any other release starts it when each user first sees it. To have it listed where
people look for packs, see [Publishing your pack](#publishing-your-pack).

## The manifest

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://maester.dev/schemas/maester-pack-1.0.json",
  "Id": "contoso.google-workspace",
  "Name": "Google Workspace checks",
  "Description": "Checks the security settings of a Google Workspace tenant.",
  "Version": "1.2.0",
  "Publisher": "contoso",
  "License": "MIT",
  "RequiresMaester": ">=3.0",
  "Code": "CNT",
  "Suites": ["tests"],
  "Helpers": ["helpers"],
  "Connectors": [
    {
      "Service": "CNT.GoogleWorkspace",
      "DisplayName": "Google Workspace",
      "File": "connector/Connect-CntGoogleWorkspace.ps1",
      "Connect": "Connect-CntGoogleWorkspace",
      "Test": "Test-CntGoogleWorkspace",
      "Disconnect": "Disconnect-CntGoogleWorkspace"
    }
  ],
  "Uses": {
    "Services": ["CNT.GoogleWorkspace"],
    "GraphScopes": [],
    "TenantWrites": [],
    "Network": ["admin.googleapis.com", "oauth2.googleapis.com"],
    "Modules": [ { "Name": "GoogleWorkspaceTools", "Version": "1.4.2" } ]
  }
}
```

| Key | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `$schema` | `https://maester.dev/schemas/maester-pack-1.0.json`, so editors such as VS Code check the manifest as you type. Maester checks it again when the pack is installed and loaded. |
| `Id` | `<publisher>.<name>` in lower case. The publisher is the GitHub user or organisation that owns the repository; a pack whose publisher is not the repository owner is refused. |
| `Guid` | Required. A GUID that identifies the pack for good, such as `d1e2db80-6c27-4cb6-9389-2edf0a898d23`; `New-MtPack` makes one. Keep it, and the code, for every version of the pack: `Update-MtPack` refuses a release whose Guid or code changed. A pack with a new code is a new pack, with a new Guid. |
| `Version` | A semantic version, such as `1.2.0`. |
| `RequiresMaester` | The Maester versions the pack works with, such as `>=3.0`. Add an upper bound, such as `>=3.0 <4.0`, only if you know a later version breaks the pack. A pack that needs a newer Maester reports `RequiresNewerMaester`. `New-MtPack` fills in the version you made the pack with. |
| `Code` | The start of every test ID of the pack: `CNT` gives `MP.CNT.1001`. Two to ten letters or digits, starting with a letter. A publisher with several packs can group them with up to three parts separated by dots, such as `CNT.GWS` for `MP.CNT.GWS.1001`. No two installed packs may share a code, or have one code that starts with the other (`CNT` and `CNT.GWS`), so `Install-MtPack` refuses the second one. Any code is allowed, but pick one that the [Maester Packs site](https://packs.maester.cloud) does not list as claimed, so people can install your pack next to others. |
| `Suites` | Folders of native tests. Each needs a `suite.json` whose `Id` is the code or starts with it, such as `CNT.GoogleWorkspace`. |
| `Helpers` | Folders of `.ps1` files that hold functions the tests call. |
| `Connectors` | Services the pack connects to (below). |
| `Uses` | What the pack reaches, shown when it is installed. An unknown key under `Uses` is an error, so a pack cannot hide what it reaches behind a key an older Maester does not show. |
| `Uses.Modules` | PowerShell Gallery modules, each pinned to one exact `Version`. Maester saves them into its own store and checks their files before every load. A module the user installs themselves can only be run in a separate process: `{ "Name": "X", "MinimumVersion": "2.0.0", "Install": "User", "Process": "Child" }`. |
| `Requires.Packs` | Other packs this one needs: `{ "Id": "contoso.base", "Source": "contoso/maester-base", "Version": ">=1.0" }`. They are installed first, with their own approval. |
| `Exports` | Functions of this pack that packs requiring it may call. |
| `Pricing` | `Free` (the default) or `Paid`, for a pack that needs a paid product or subscription to be useful. The pack index shows it; Maester does not act on it. |
| `Banner` | An image in the pack that the pack index shows when it features the pack. See [Banner image](#banner-image). |
| `Guide` | A JSON file in the pack that says how to install, connect and run it, for its page on the pack index. See [The pack page](#the-pack-page). |
| `Report.Navigation` | The pack's menu in the Maester report. See [The pack's menu in the report](#the-packs-menu-in-the-report). |
| `EnabledByDefault` | For a pack that ships with Maester: `false` to leave it off until the config turns it on. |

## Banner image

A banner is optional. When the maintainers feature a pack on [packs.maester.cloud](https://packs.maester.cloud), the
card shows the banner beside the pack's description; without one, the card shows the pack's code and name on a dark
background.

- **File:** `.png`, `.jpg` or `.webp`, at most 1 MB, inside the pack, for example `"Banner": "assets/banner.png"`.
  The index reads the type from the file's contents, not its name, and SVG is refused. A banner that fails these
  checks is left out and the card falls back to the code and name.
- **Size:** 1200 × 630 pixels (the 1.91:1 shape of a social preview). Another size is cropped to fill that shape.
- **Shown small:** about 600 pixels wide on a desktop and 340 on a phone. Use at most eight words of text, set large,
  and keep it away from the edges.
- **Your own brand.** Use another company's logo only for a pack built on that company's product, and only with its
  permission. Don't add words such as "Official" or "Verified": the index shows its own badges, and a banner that
  suggests an endorsement it doesn't have can get the pack removed.
- **No secrets or real data:** a screenshot must not show a real tenant, user or key.

### Making one with an AI image tool

Any image tool that takes a text prompt can make a banner. Image tools often misspell words, so check every letter,
or ask for an image with no text and add the title yourself in an editor. Fill in the parts in angle brackets:

```text
A wide banner image, 1200 x 630 pixels, for a software add-on called "<pack name>".
It checks the security settings of <service, for example Google Workspace> for IT administrators.
Style: clean, modern, flat illustration on a <dark navy / deep teal / near-black> gradient background,
with a simple abstract motif suggesting <what the pack checks, for example identity, email, devices>.
Text: the title "<pack name>" in large, bold, white sans-serif letters on the left,
and the line "<one short phrase, at most six words>" below it in smaller letters.
Leave a margin of at least 60 pixels on every side. No other text, no logos, no people,
no photos of screens, no badges or seals.
```

For an image without text, replace the `Text:` line with `No text at all; leave the left half plain for a title.`

## The pack page

Every pack's page on [packs.maester.cloud](https://packs.maester.cloud) has the same sections: Install, Connect,
Run, App-only, Tests, Security and Support. The index fills what it can from the manifest:

- the modules in `Uses.Modules`, with the line that installs each one;
- the Graph permissions in `Uses.GraphScopes`, which an app needs to run the pack app-only;
- the tests, with their products, from `Suites` (and `Catalog` for a family test that expands when it runs).

The rest comes from the Guide, a JSON file in the pack named by the manifest's `Guide` key, such as
`"Guide": "maester-pack.guide.json"`. Its schema is
[maester-pack-guide-1.0.json](https://maester.dev/schemas/maester-pack-guide-1.0.json); add it as `$schema` so
editors check the file as you type. Commands in it are shown as text and never run. A short example:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://maester.dev/schemas/maester-pack-guide-1.0.json",
  "Summary": "Checks the security settings of Google Workspace.",
  "Prerequisites": [{ "Text": "A Google Workspace super admin account." }],
  "Connect": { "Steps": [{ "Text": "Connect Maester, then sign in to Google when asked", "Command": "Connect-Maester" }] },
  "Run": {
    "Commands": [{ "Text": "Only this pack", "Command": "Invoke-Maester -Pack CNT -SkipBuiltIn" }],
    "Options": [{ "Name": "GoogleWorkspace.Customer", "Default": "my_customer", "Text": "The customer ID to read." }]
  },
  "AppOnly": { "Supported": true, "Methods": { "Certificate": true, "ClientSecret": true }, "Text": "Use a service account key." },
  "Screenshots": [{ "Path": "assets/report.png", "Caption": "The pack's results in the Maester report" }],
  "Support": { "Pack": "https://github.com/contoso/maester-google-workspace/issues" }
}
```

Maester checks that the Guide is a JSON object and that its screenshots (at most six) are `.png`, `.jpg` or `.webp`
paths inside the pack. Like the banner, a screenshot that really is an image of at most 1 MB is not counted as
binary content. Any section can end with `"More": "<https link>"` to your own documentation. The
[Zero Trust Assessment pack's guide](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/packs/zero-trust-assessment/maester-pack.guide.json)
is a full example.

## The pack's menu in the report

To show a logo in the header of the pack's page instead of its `Code`, set `Report.Logo` to a mark the report draws
itself: `microsoft`, or a product key such as `entra` or `defender`. The report never loads an image from a pack, and
a name it does not know shows the `Code`. The icon on the menu's rail always shows the `Code`.

```json
"Report": { "Logo": "microsoft" }
```

In the Maester report, each pack has a row on the home menu. Selecting it opens the pack's own menu beside an icon
rail, as a resource menu does in the Azure portal. Without a `Report.Navigation` key, the menu has an overview, one
page for each value of the first field your tests set in `Fields`, the HTML reports your tests attached, the guide's
pages and an About page.

To choose the menu yourself, list its entries. An entry is a row (`Title`) or a heading (`Section`) that opens one of
the report's own views. Any entry can hold `Items`, to any depth:

```json
"Report": {
  "Navigation": [
    { "Title": "Overview", "View": "pack" },
    { "Section": "Zero Trust plan", "Id": "plan", "View": "plan", "Attachment": "zero-trust-workshop", "Expand": ["pillars", "areas", "lanes"] },
    { "Section": "Assessment results", "Items": [
      { "Title": "All results", "Id": "results", "View": "tests" },
      { "Title": "Not met", "Id": "not-met", "View": "tests", "Result": "Failed" },
      { "Title": "By pillar", "Id": "by-pillar", "View": "tests", "GroupBy": ["Pillar", "Category"] },
      { "Title": "Assessment report", "View": "attachment", "Attachment": "Zero Trust Assessment" }
    ] },
    { "Title": "About this pack", "Id": "about", "View": "about" }
  ]
}
```

| View | What the page shows | Keys |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pack` | The pack's overview: who publishes it, how its tests did, and its results. | |
| `tests` | The pack's results. `GroupBy` adds a menu level for each field it names: `["Pillar", "Category"]` lists each pillar, and each pillar's categories under it. | `Result`, `Filter` (field names to a value or a list of values), `GroupBy` |
| `plan` | A JSON attachment drawn by a view the report ships. Today that is the Zero Trust Workshop plan (`maester.zero-trust-workshop/1`). `Expand` lists its levels in the menu. | `Attachment`, `Expand` |
| `attachment` | An HTML report a test attached with `Add-MtReportAttachment`. | `Attachment` (the `-Name` you gave it) |
| `guide` | A page of the pack's [Guide](#the-pack-page): `start` (summary, prerequisites and links), `connect` or `run`. | `Page` |
| `about` | The pack's ID, version, publisher, status in the run and home page. | |

`Id` is the entry's part of the page's link (`#/pack/<code>/<id>`); without it, the report uses the title in lower
case with dashes. Keep it stable, so that links people share keep working.

Nothing in the menu runs: the report draws only its own views, so a pack never adds code to the report people share.
Maester refuses a manifest whose menu is malformed, such as an entry with neither a `Title` nor a `Section`, or a
`plan` entry without its `Attachment`. A view or key it does not know is only a warning, and the report leaves that
entry out, so a pack written for a newer Maester still loads. Maester also warns about a menu more than five levels
deep: each level indents the menu and shortens its labels.

## Tests and helpers

A pack's tests are [native tests](../writing-tests/index.mdx) with IDs `MP.<Code>.<n>`, or `MP.<Code>` for a family whose instances add their own part. (Packs that ship with
Maester are part of it and drop the `MP.`: the Zero Trust Assessment pack's tests are `ZTA.<n>`.) Every `.ps1` in a suite
or helper folder holds only functions: code outside a function is refused, because it would run while the pack
loads. A pack loads into a private module of its own, so its tests can call its helpers and Maester's exported
commands. One pack does not see another pack's functions unless it requires that pack and the pack lists them in
`Exports`. This keeps cooperating packs from colliding; it is not a security boundary, because code in the same
PowerShell process can reach anything in it (see [Pack security](./security.md)).

The scan flags, and raises the risk of, what a reviewer should look at: binary files, dynamic code
(`Invoke-Expression`, `[scriptblock]::Create`), starting processes, requests to hosts that `Uses.Network` does not
list, and module imports that `Uses.Modules` does not list.

### Mapping a pack's results to a framework

A pack test maps itself to a requirement with `Control`, like any test (see
[Benchmarks and framework files](../writing-tests/index.mdx#benchmarks-and-framework-files)). It can name a
framework that ships with Maester, such as `cisa-scuba`, or one that the pack's own `suite.json` declares. A family
whose instances each report on a different requirement sets `Control` on each instance instead, with the other
attributes an instance may set (see [Families](../writing-tests/index.mdx#families-one-test-several-results)):

```powershell
foreach ($policy in $scubaResults) {
    @{ Id = $policy.PolicyId; Title = $policy.Requirement; Control = "cisa-scuba:$($policy.PolicyId)"; Data = $policy }
}
```

Each row then has its own `Benchmark`, and the report's framework view shows the pack's result under the
requirement next to any Maester test that names the same one.

## Showing a long-running test's output and progress

A test that runs a tool for a long time, such as an assessment in another PowerShell process, can show the person
running Maester what the tool is doing while it runs. In the full-screen dashboard both go into a box in the main
column; in the compact layout, CI and redirected output they are written to the console, indented.

- `Write-MtTestOutput` shows the tool's log. `-Title` opens the box, each line
  scrolls into it, `-Progress` pins a changing line at the bottom, and `-Complete` closes it (Maester closes it when
  the test ends).
- `Write-MtTestProgress` shows where the tool is, as a header at the top of
  the box: the stage (`-Stage`, `-StageNumber`, `-StageCount`), a bar of the items done (`-Completed`, `-Total`,
  `-Failed`, `-Running`), what it is working on (`-Current`, `-Status`), and the errors it reported
  (`-ErrorMessage`), which the box also counts. With `-Stages` (the names of all the stages) the stages are drawn
  as a track, like the phases of a Maester run. With `-Items` (each with `Id`, and optionally `Title`, `Status`,
  `Detail` and `Seconds`) the box lists the items running and those that finished, with their result and time,
  the way the dashboard lists Maester's own tests; outside the dashboard each finished item is written once. Each
  call replaces the progress before it, so pass everything you know each time; a call with only `-ErrorMessage`
  keeps the progress.
- When the tool runs tests of its own, `-Results` (`Passed`, `Failed`, `Error`, `Investigate`, `Skipped`,
  `Running`, `Total` and optionally `Name`) and `-Groups` (the same counts with a `Name` each, such as the pillars
  of an assessment, with `-GroupLabel 'Zero Trust Pillars'`) show them in the dashboard in place of Maester's own while the
  box is open: in the Results panel and the result blocks, and where the products are listed. The times of the
  items that finished go into the Pace graph next to the logo and the Slowest panel.

```powershell
Write-MtTestOutput -Title 'Collecting the tenant data'
Write-MtTestProgress -Stage 'Exporting' -StageNumber 1 -StageCount 3 -Completed 12 -Total 40 -Running 2 -Current 'Users', 'Groups'
Write-MtTestProgress -ErrorMessage 'The export of Devices failed: Forbidden'
```

A tool in another process does not need to call Maester to report its progress. Pipe its output to
`Write-MtTestOutput`, and have it write lines of this form to standard output, from any language:

```text
##maester[progress] {"stages":["Export","Tests","Report"],"stageNumber":1,"stage":"Exporting","completed":12,"total":40,"failed":1,"items":[{"id":"Users","detail":"page 3","seconds":12},{"id":"Groups","status":"Passed","seconds":4.2}]}
##maester[progress] {"stage":"Running tests","results":{"passed":80,"failed":12,"running":4,"total":300},"groupLabel":"Zero Trust Pillars","groups":[{"name":"Identity","passed":50,"failed":8,"total":120}]}
##maester[error] The export of Devices failed: Forbidden
```

These lines set the header instead of showing in the log. The JSON object takes the names of the parameters of
`Write-MtTestProgress` in any case (`error` for `-ErrorMessage`), and leaves out what it does not know. Write a
`progress` line when something changes (at most a few times a second): each one is drawn. A line that cannot be read is dropped.

The [Zero Trust Assessment pack](./zero-trust-assessment.md) is a worked example: its child process reads the
progress the assessment keeps and the progress logs it writes, once a second, and writes these lines (see
`Invoke-MtZtaCollection` in `packs/zero-trust-assessment/tests/Test.ZTA.ps1`).

## Connectors

A connector adds a service to Maester. Its file holds a `Connect` and a `Test` function, and optionally
`Disconnect`, `Renew` and `Describe`:

```powershell
function Connect-CntGoogleWorkspace {
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([string] $Domain, [string] $CredentialPath)

    $token = Get-CntAccessToken -Domain $Domain -CredentialPath $CredentialPath
    Set-MtConnectionState -Value @{ Token = $token.AccessToken; ExpiresOn = $token.ExpiresOn } -Tenant $Domain
}

function Test-CntGoogleWorkspace {
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()
    [bool](Get-MtConnectionState)
}
```

- `Connect-Maester -Service CNT.GoogleWorkspace` calls `Connect` with the parameters it has from `-ServiceSetting`,
  `MAESTER_CNT_GOOGLEWORKSPACE_<PARAMETER>` and `Connections.CNT.GoogleWorkspace` in the config.
- `Set-MtConnectionState` keeps what the tests need for the PowerShell session only; `Get-MtConnectionState`
  reads it back in a test or helper. A pack can read its own connection and those of packs it requires, never
  another pack's.
- `Test` decides whether the tests that need the service run. With `ExpiresOn` in the state, Maester calls `Renew`
  shortly before it expires.
- The service name is `<Code>.<Name>`. Tests declare it like any service: `Service = 'CNT.GoogleWorkspace'`.
  `"OptIn": true` makes its tests not run, rather than skipped, while it is not connected.

## Publishing your pack

Once the pack has a release, anyone can install it from its repository with `Install-MtPack <owner>/<repo>`. To
help people find it, list it on a pack index: a site that collects packs, checks them and shows each one's page.
An index only lists a pack. People still install it straight from your repository, and Maester runs the same checks
at install whichever site they found it on.

### Maester Packs

[packs.maester.cloud](https://packs.maester.cloud/) is the index the Maester team runs. To list a pack there:

1. Go to [packs.maester.cloud/publish](https://packs.maester.cloud/publish) and choose
   **Yes, I have a pack repository**.
2. Sign in with GitHub as an admin of the repository. The repository must be public; private and internal
   repositories are never listed.
3. Pick the repository, and the folder if the pack is not at its root, then press **Check**. It reads the latest
   release and its `maester-pack.json`, and says what to fix.
4. Press **Publish**. The site registers the pack's `Guid` and `Code` to the repository's owner, so nobody else can
   publish a pack with them, and queues the pack.

Within about ten minutes the index runs `Test-MtPack`'s checks and its security scan on the release and lists the
pack, with its page at `/p/<code>`. If the pack is not listed, its status page at `/status/<owner>/<repo>` says why
and what to fix. Every later release is picked up on its own, so you publish only once. **My Packs** on the site
shows your packs and how many tenants run them, and lets you hide one from the site for a while.

function Get-ScubaGwsInstance {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Returns one MP.SCUBA.GWS instance per policy result in a ScubaGoggles ScubaResults file.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Instance source of the MP.SCUBA.GWS family. Reads the ScubaResults JSON that the scubagoggles gws command wrote,
    from the ScubaGoggles.ReportPath setting, and returns one instance per result. Skips the whole family, with
    the reason, when the setting is empty, the file is not found or the report is too old.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param()

    $reportPath = [string](Get-MtSetting -Name 'ScubaGoggles.ReportPath' -Default '')
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($reportPath)) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason 'No ScubaGoggles report to read. Run scubagoggles gws, then set the ScubaGoggles.ReportPath setting to the ScubaResults file or the folder it wrote.'
    }

    $file = Resolve-ScubaGwsResultFile -Path $reportPath
    $report = Get-Content -LiteralPath $file -Raw -Encoding utf8 | ConvertFrom-Json -Depth 20
    if (-not $report.PSObject.Properties['Results'] -or -not $report.PSObject.Properties['MetaData']) {
        throw "$file is not a ScubaGoggles results file: it has no MetaData or Results."
    }
    if ([string]$report.MetaData.Tool -ne 'ScubaGoggles') {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason "$file was written by $($report.MetaData.Tool), not ScubaGoggles."
    }

    $maxAgeDays = [int](Get-MtSetting -Name 'ScubaGoggles.MaxReportAgeDays' -Default 7)
    # ConvertFrom-Json reads the ISO date as a DateTime already; text is parsed invariantly, never in the current culture.
    $written = [datetime]::MinValue
    $hasDate = if ($report.MetaData.TimestampZulu -is [datetime]) { $written = $report.MetaData.TimestampZulu; $true }
    else {
        [datetime]::TryParse([string]$report.MetaData.TimestampZulu, [cultureinfo]::InvariantCulture,
            [System.Globalization.DateTimeStyles]::AdjustToUniversal -bor [System.Globalization.DateTimeStyles]::AssumeUniversal, [ref]$written)
    }
    if ($maxAgeDays -gt 0 -and $hasDate -and $written.ToUniversalTime() -lt [datetime]::UtcNow.AddDays(-$maxAgeDays)) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason "The ScubaGoggles report at $file was written on $($written.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd')), more than $maxAgeDays days ago. Run scubagoggles gws again, or raise the ScubaGoggles.MaxReportAgeDays setting."
    }

    ConvertTo-ScubaGwsInstance -Report $report -Catalog (Get-ScubaGwsCatalog)
}

```

The built-in check functions are no longer exported in 3.0, and they no longer contain their own connection
checks, so calling one directly is not supported.

## A suite manifest for your folder

A `suite.json` in a test folder sets what is true for every test in it (and its subfolders, unless a nearer
`suite.json` exists):

```json
{
  "Id": "Contoso",
  "Name": "Contoso security baseline",
  "Source": "Custom",
  "Tags": ["Contoso"],
  "HelpUrlTemplate": "https://wiki.contoso.com/maester/{Id}",
  "RequiresMaester": "3.0"
}
```

| Key | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `Id` | Written to each result row as `Suite`, which `-Suite` selects by. Defaults to `Custom`. |
| `Name` | The `Block` of the result rows of tests that have neither `Product` nor `Feature`. |
| `Source` | Written to each result row as `Source`. Defaults to `Custom`. |
| `Tags` | Matched by `-Tag` and `-ExcludeTag` for every test in the folder. Not written to the result rows. |
| `HelpUrlTemplate` | The `HelpUrl` of tests that do not set one; `{Id}` is replaced. |
| `RequiresMaester` | Tests in the folder need at least this Maester version. On an older version each one is an `Error` row with reason `RequiresNewerMaester`. |
| `NoResultReason` | The skip text shown when a test returns `$null` without calling `Add-MtTestResultDetail`. Defaults to "The test returned no result." |
| `Frameworks` | The frameworks whose catalogue is in the folder. See [Benchmarks and framework files](#benchmarks-and-framework-files). |

A single file can state the same as `RequiresMaester` with
`#Requires -Modules @{ ModuleName = 'Maester'; ModuleVersion = '3.1' }`.

### Benchmarks and framework files

A test says which requirement of a framework it implements in its own attribute, with `Control`:

```powershell
[MaesterTest(
    Id      = 'CONTOSO.BL.1.1',
    Title   = 'Admins sign in with phishing-resistant MFA',
    Control = 'contoso-baseline:1.1'
)]
```

A `Control` value is `<framework-key>:<requirement-id>`. This is the only way a test is mapped to a framework. It
is the same for the CIS, CISA and ASD tests that ship with Maester (`Control = 'cis-m365:5.1.5.1'`,
`Control = 'cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1'`, `Control = 'essential-eight:ISM-1504'`) and for a test of your own.

The frameworks that ship with Maester, with the key to use in `Control`:

| Key | Framework | Framework file | Declared in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cis-m365` | CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations Benchmark | [tests/cis/frameworks/cis-m365.json](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/tests/cis/frameworks/cis-m365.json) | [tests/cis/suite.json](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/tests/cis/suite.json) |
| `cis-github` | CIS GitHub Benchmark | [tests/cis/frameworks/cis-github.json](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/tests/cis/frameworks/cis-github.json) | [tests/cis/suite.json](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/tests/cis/suite.json) |
| `cisa-scuba` | CISA SCuBA Secure Configuration Baselines for Microsoft 365 | [tests/cisa/frameworks/cisa-scuba.json](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/tests/cisa/frameworks/cisa-scuba.json) | [tests/cisa/suite.json](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/tests/cisa/suite.json) |
| `essential-eight` | ASD Essential Eight maturity model (each requirement is an ISM control; `Level` ML1 to ML3, `Strategy`) | [tests/asd/frameworks/essential-eight.json](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/tests/asd/frameworks/essential-eight.json) | [tests/asd/suite.json](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/tests/asd/suite.json) |
| `ism` | ASD Information security manual (ISM) (`Guideline`, `Section`, `Applicability`) | [tests/asd/frameworks/ism.json](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/tests/asd/frameworks/ism.json) | [tests/asd/suite.json](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/tests/asd/suite.json) |

Open a file to see the requirement IDs you can reference and the version Maester implements. NIST SP 800-53 has
no framework file; its control IDs are in
[powershell/assets/MaesterNistControls.json](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/powershell/assets/MaesterNistControls.json)
and are written `nist-800-53-r5:<control>`. The [test builder](/test-builder) looks all of them up.

A framework file is the catalogue of one framework: its name, its version and every requirement, with the facts
about each. A suite that holds a framework file declares it in its `suite.json`:

```json
{
  "Id": "Contoso",
  "Name": "Contoso security baseline",
  "Frameworks": [
    { "Key": "contoso-baseline", "Version": "2.1" }
  ]
}
```

| Key | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `Key` | The key of the framework: lowercase letters, digits, dots and hyphens. It names the framework file, it is the first part of a `Control` value, and it is written to the result. |
| `Version` | The version of the framework. When omitted, the `Version` of the framework file is used. |

The file is `frameworks/<Key>.json`, beside the `suite.json`:

```json
{
  "Framework": "contoso-baseline",
  "Name": "Contoso Security Baseline",
  "Version": "2.1",
  "Url": "https://wiki.contoso.com/baseline",
  "Requirements": [
    { "Id": "1.1", "Level": "L1", "Related": ["nist-800-53-r5:IA-2(1)"] },
    { "Id": "1.2", "Level": "L2" }
  ]
}
```

- `Framework` is the `Key` from the `suite.json`. `Name` is the name of the framework and `Url` is where it is
  published. A `Version` here must be the one the `suite.json` declares.
- A requirement has an `Id`, written as a string. It is the second part of a `Control` value, and it is matched
  exactly, including upper and lower case.
- `Related` lists controls of other frameworks that the requirement relates to, written
  `<framework-key>:<control-id>` with a lowercase key, like a `Control` value.
- Any other key is a fact about the requirement, such as `Level`, `Profile` or `Criticality`. Keep to identifiers
  and facts. Do not copy the text of a benchmark into the file: it is often licensed, and the test's own title
  already says what is checked.
- The file does not list tests. A `Tests` key on a requirement and an `IdPrefix` key in the `suite.json` are
  ignored.

#### What the result gets

Maester looks up each `Control` value of a test, in the order they are written. A value resolves when its key is
a framework that has a file and its ID is a requirement in that file.

- `Benchmark` is built from the first value that resolves: the `Framework`, its `Version`, the `Requirement` and
  the requirement's own facts. When no value resolves, `Benchmark` is `null`.
- `Control` holds the values the test wrote, followed by the `Related` references of every requirement that
  resolved, each once.

`Get-MtTest` shows both. See [the result schema](../result-schema.md#benchmark).

An instance of a [family](#families-one-test-several-results) can set its own `Control`, resolved the same way against the frameworks its
family can name. A report lists every row that names a requirement under it, so when a pack's instance and a
Maester test name the same requirement, both are shown.

A framework is found by its key, whatever suite declares it. A custom test can name a framework that ships with
Maester (`cis-m365`, `cis-github`, `cisa-scuba`, `essential-eight`, `ism`) or one that a suite in your own test folder declares. Two suites
must not declare the same key: Maester warns, names both `suite.json` files and uses the first, and a framework
that ships with Maester comes before one of yours.

A `Control` value whose key no framework file has, such as `nist-800-53-r5:IA-2(1)` or `iso-27001-2022:A.5.17`,
is written to the result as it is. It needs no file.

A problem with a framework never stops a run. Maester writes a warning that names the file and what is wrong:

- The file is missing or is not valid JSON, its `Framework` or `Version` differs from the `suite.json`, a
  requirement has no `Id` or an `Id` that is listed twice, or a `Related` reference is not written
  `<framework-key>:<control-id>`. No test gets a `Benchmark` or `Related` controls from that framework.
- A `Control` names a framework that has a file and a requirement that is not in it, usually a typing error. That
  value gives no `Benchmark`; the other tests keep theirs.

#### Mapping a test to a framework

| The test | What to write | What the result gets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Implements a requirement of a benchmark that has a framework file (`CIS.M365.5.1.5.1`, `CONTOSO.BL.1.1`) | `Control = 'cis-m365:5.1.5.1'`. If the requirement is new, add it to the framework file. | `Benchmark`, and the reference in `Control` |
| Exists for its own reasons and also supports such a requirement (a Maester test that checks what a CISA policy asks for) | `Control = 'cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1'` | The same |
| Supports a control of a framework that has no file | `Control = 'nist-800-53-r5:IA-2(1)'` | The reference in `Control` |

A test can list several values. Put the requirement the test is written for first: the first value that resolves
becomes the `Benchmark`. Use the keys and requirement IDs of the framework files that ship with Maester so your
results line up with the built-in ones. For a framework that has no file, choose a lowercase key such as
`nist-800-53-r5` or `iso-27001-2022` and keep to it.

#### Why the framework file still exists

A `key:id` string names a requirement. It cannot hold what is true of the requirement whatever test implements

﻿function Set-MtConnectionState {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Keeps the connection of a Maester Pack connector for the session, so its tests and Connect-Maester can find it.

    .DESCRIPTION
    A pack connector calls this from its Connect function (Maester Packs design, section 6.1). The state is
    kept by Maester, per service, in the PowerShell session only: it is never written to disk or to the
    report. The tests of the pack read it back with Get-MtConnectionState, and Disconnect-Maester clears it.

    The service is the connector's own: the one whose Connect function is running, or the only connector
    of the calling pack. A pack can set the state of its own services only; called from outside a pack,
    -Service is required.

    Put an access token's expiry in the value as ExpiresOn (a date) to have Maester call the connector's
    Renew function shortly before it expires.

    .PARAMETER Value
    What the pack needs to reach the service: a token, a client object or settings. Kept as it is.

    .PARAMETER Account
    The account or identity that is connected, shown by Get-MtTenantContext and in the report header.

    .PARAMETER Tenant
    The tenant, organisation or workspace that is connected, shown with the account.

    .PARAMETER Service
    The connector's service name, such as CNT.GoogleWorkspace. Needed only outside the connector's own
    Connect function when the pack has more than one connector.

    .EXAMPLE
    Set-MtConnectionState -Value @{ Token = $token; ExpiresOn = $expiresOn } -Account $user -Tenant $domain

    Inside a pack connector's Connect function: keeps the token for the pack's tests.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/commands/Set-MtConnectionState
    #>
    [CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory, Position = 0)]
        [AllowNull()]
        [object] $Value,

        [Parameter()]
        [string] $Account,

        [Parameter()]
        [string] $Tenant,

        [Parameter()]
        [string] $Service
    )

    Write-Verbose "Set-MtConnectionState: Service=$Service Account=$Account"

    $resolved = Resolve-MtConnectionStateService -Service $Service -SessionState $PSCmdlet.SessionState -Write
    if (-not $PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess($resolved, 'Keep the connection state')) { return }
    if (-not $__MtSession.PackConnections) { $__MtSession.PackConnections = @{} }
    $__MtSession.PackConnections[$resolved] = [pscustomobject]@{
        Service     = $resolved
        Value       = $Value
        Account     = $Account
        Tenant      = $Tenant
        ConnectedAt = [datetime]::UtcNow
    }
}
﻿function Get-MtConnectionState {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Returns what a Maester Pack connector kept with Set-MtConnectionState, or nothing when it is not connected.

    .DESCRIPTION
    A pack's tests and helpers call this to reach the service their connector connected to (Maester Packs
    design, section 6.1). Inside a pack, it returns the state of the pack's own connector, or of a pack it
    requires; one pack cannot read another pack's connection. Called from outside a pack, -Service is
    required.

    By default the value the connector kept is returned. -Detailed returns Service, Value, Account, Tenant
    and ConnectedAt.

    .PARAMETER Service
    The connector's service name, such as CNT.GoogleWorkspace. Needed only when the pack has more than one
    connector, or outside a pack.

    .PARAMETER Detailed
    Return the whole record: Service, Value, Account, Tenant and ConnectedAt.

    .EXAMPLE
    $token = (Get-MtConnectionState).Token

    Inside a pack test: the token the pack's connector kept.

    .EXAMPLE
    Get-MtConnectionState -Service CNT.GoogleWorkspace -Detailed

    At the console: who is connected to the service of an installed pack.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/commands/Get-MtConnectionState
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([object])]
    param(
        [Parameter(Position = 0)]
        [string] $Service,

        [Parameter()]
        [switch] $Detailed
    )

    Write-Verbose "Get-MtConnectionState: Service=$Service"

    $resolved = Resolve-MtConnectionStateService -Service $Service -SessionState $PSCmdlet.SessionState
    if (-not $__MtSession.PackConnections -or -not $__MtSession.PackConnections.ContainsKey($resolved)) { return }
    $state = $__MtSession.PackConnections[$resolved]
    if ($Detailed) { $state } else { $state.Value }
}

Describe 'ScubaGoggles pack' {
    BeforeAll {
        $maester = if ($env:MAESTER_MODULE) { $env:MAESTER_MODULE } else { 'Maester' }
        Import-Module $maester -Force -WarningAction SilentlyContinue
        $script:PackRoot = (Resolve-Path "$PSScriptRoot/..").Path

        # policies.
        $script:Fixture = (Resolve-Path "$PSScriptRoot/fixtures").Path
        $script:FixtureFile = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $script:Fixture -Filter 'ScubaResults*.json' -File -Recurse | Select-Object -First 1 -ExpandProperty FullName

        function Invoke-ScubaGogglesPack {
            param([hashtable] $Setting = @{})
            $globalSettings = @{ 'ScubaGoggles.ReportPath' = $script:Fixture; 'ScubaGoggles.MaxReportAgeDays' = 0 }
            foreach ($key in $Setting.Keys) { $globalSettings[$key] = $Setting[$key] }
            $config = [pscustomobject]@{ GlobalSettings = [pscustomobject]$globalSettings }
            @(Invoke-MtTest -Path $script:TestsPath -Id MP.SCUBA.GWS -Config $config)
        }

        $script:Rows = Invoke-ScubaGogglesPack
    }

    Context 'the pack files' {
        It 'has a valid native test' {
            $test = Get-MtTest -Path (Join-Path $script:TestsPath 'Test.MP.SCUBA.GWS.ps1')
            $test.IsValid | Should -BeTrue
            $test.Errors | Should -BeNullOrEmpty
            $test.InstanceSource | Should -Be 'Get-ScubaGwsInstance'
        }

        It 'has a catalog of unique policy IDs with their text' {
            $catalog = Get-Content (Join-Path $script:PackRoot 'catalog.json') -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
            $catalog.Version | Should -Not -BeNullOrEmpty
            $catalog.Tests.Count | Should -BeGreaterThan 0
            @($catalog.Tests.Id | Where-Object { $_ -notmatch '^MP\.SCUBA\.GWS\.[A-Z]+\.\d+\.\d+$' }) | Should -BeNullOrEmpty
            @($catalog.Tests.Id | Sort-Object -Unique).Count | Should -Be $catalog.Tests.Count
            @($catalog.Tests | Where-Object { -not $_.Title -or -not $_.Rationale -or -not $_.Remediation -or $_.Criticality -notin 'SHALL', 'SHOULD', 'MAY' }).ControlId | Should -BeNullOrEmpty
        }
    }

    Context 'reading results' {
        It 'writes one row per result' {
            $script:Rows.Count | Should -Be 13
        }

        It 'maps <Id> to <Result>' -ForEach @(

            @{ Id = 'MP.SCUBA.GWS.CALENDAR.1.1'; Result = 'Failed' }             # Fail, a SHALL policy
            @{ Id = 'MP.SCUBA.GWS.ASSUREDCONTROLS.2.1'; Result = 'Failed' }      # Warning, a SHOULD policy
            @{ Id = 'MP.SCUBA.GWS.COMMONCONTROLS.2.1'; Result = 'Investigate' }  # No events found
            @{ Id = 'MP.SCUBA.GWS.CALENDAR.3.2'; Result = 'Skipped' }            # N/A
            @{ Id = 'MP.SCUBA.GWS.GMAIL.4.1'; Result = 'Skipped' }               # Omitted

# CISA ScubaGoggles pack for Maester

A [Maester Pack](https://maester.dev/docs/next/packs) that shows the results of
[ScubaGoggles](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles) in the Maester report. ScubaGoggles is CISA's free tool
that checks a Google Workspace tenant against the Secure Cloud Business Applications (SCuBA) baselines for Google
Workspace: Gmail, Drive and Docs, Common Controls, Calendar, Chat, Meet, Groups, Sites, Classroom, Gemini and
Assured Controls.

Each policy is one row, `MP.SCUBA.GWS.<product>.<group>.<policy>`: `GWS.GMAIL.1.1v1` is `MP.SCUBA.GWS.GMAIL.1.1`.
The ID leaves out the policy's version, so a row keeps its ID when CISA updates the policy. Each row has the
policy's requirement as its title, the baseline's rationale, the steps to configure it, its NIST SP 800-53 and
MITRE ATT&CK mappings, and what ScubaGoggles found. Rows are tagged `SCuBA` and `SCuBA.<baseline>`
(`SCuBA.GMAIL`, `SCuBA.DRIVEDOCS` and so on, as in the ScubaGear pack), and policies that BOD 25-01 requires are
tagged `BOD-25-01`. Each row carries the MITRE ATT&CK techniques CISA maps the policy to.

The pack does not sign in to Google or run ScubaGoggles: you run ScubaGoggles, and the pack reads the results file
it wrote. It needs Maester 3.0.0-rc59 or later.

## Run it

Install ScubaGoggles once, with Python 3.11 or later:

```bash
pip install scubagoggles
scubagoggles setup
```

`scubagoggles setup` downloads [Open Policy Agent](https://www.openpolicyagent.org/), which ScubaGoggles uses to
evaluate the policies, and saves the output folder and the credentials file. ScubaGoggles signs in with a Google
OAuth client and a super admin, or with a service account that has domain-wide delegation; its
[authentication guide](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles/blob/main/docs/authentication/AuthenticationMethods.md)
says how to set up either one.

Run the assessment:

```bash
scubagoggles gws -o ./scubagoggles
```

Install the pack, point it at the output folder in `maester-config.json`, and run it:

```powershell
Install-MtPack maester365/maester-pack-scubagoggles
```

Every release of the pack, newest first. Install-MtPack shows the version; Update-MtPack moves to a newer one.

## 0.1.0

- The first release: reads the ScubaResults file of ScubaGoggles 1.1.0 and reports each of its 138 Google

# Security

Report a security problem in this pack privately, through
[GitHub's private vulnerability reporting](https://github.com/maester365/maester-pack-scubagoggles/security/advisories/new),
not in a public issue. The same link is the pack's `SecurityContact` in `maester-pack.json`.

A problem in ScubaGoggles goes to [cisagov/ScubaGoggles](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles/security), and one
in Maester itself to [maester365/maester](https://github.com/maester365/maester/security).
# Publishes a release for the version on main. After each push to main (a merged pull request), it reads Version
# from maester-pack.json and, when there is no release v<Version> yet, tags that commit v<Version> and publishes a
# release with the version's section of CHANGELOG.md as its notes. Install-MtPack installs the newest published
# release once it is older than the install cooldown. A merge with release:none keeps the version, so it
# publishes nothing. Run it by hand (workflow_dispatch) to publish the version on main if a run was missed.
#
# It runs only when the repository variable PACK_RELEASES is true, with bump-version.yml. Without it the pack has
# no releases and Install-MtPack installs the default branch. See "Versions and releases" in README.md.
name: Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: release

jobs:
  release:
    if: vars.PACK_RELEASES == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Publish the release
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          $version = [string](Get-Content -LiteralPath maester-pack.json -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json).Version
          if ($version -notmatch '^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$') { throw "Version '$version' in maester-pack.json is not major.minor.patch." }

function Connect-JamfPro {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Connects the pack to a Jamf Pro server with an API client, or with a Jamf Pro account.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Connect-Maester -Service JAMF.JamfPro calls this. Its parameters come from -ServiceSetting, from
    Connections.JAMF.JamfPro in maester-config.json, or from MAESTER_JAMF_JAMFPRO_<NAME> environment variables,
    such as MAESTER_JAMF_JAMFPRO_CLIENTSECRET.

    Use an API client (Settings > System > API roles and clients) with a role that only reads: the pack's README
    lists the privileges. A Jamf Pro account with a user name and password works too, for servers older than
    10.49 or a quick try.

    The token, and the client secret or password needed to get a new one, are kept for this PowerShell session
    only. Maester asks for a new token shortly before the old one expires.

    .PARAMETER Server
    The Jamf Pro address, such as https://contoso.jamfcloud.com or jamf.contoso.com:8443.

    .PARAMETER ClientId
    The client ID of the Jamf Pro API client.

    .PARAMETER ClientSecret
    The client secret of the API client. Prefer the MAESTER_JAMF_JAMFPRO_CLIENTSECRET environment variable to
    writing it in a file.

    .PARAMETER Username
    A Jamf Pro account, instead of an API client.

    .PARAMETER Password
    The password of that account.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Server,
        [Parameter()] [string] $ClientId,
        [Parameter()] [string] $ClientSecret,
        [Parameter()] [string] $Username,
        [Parameter()] [string] $Password
    )

    $baseUri = ConvertTo-JamfServerUri -Server $Server
    $state = @{
        Server       = $baseUri
        ClientId     = $ClientId
        ClientSecret = REDACTED
        Username     = $Username
        Password     = $Password
        Cache        = @{}
    }
    if ($ClientId -and $ClientSecret) { $state.Method = 'ApiClient' }
    elseif ($Username -and $Password) { $state.Method = 'Account' }
    else { throw 'Give Connect-JamfPro a ClientId and ClientSecret (an API client), or a Username and Password.' }

    Update-JamfProToken -State $state
    $account = if ($state.Method -eq 'ApiClient') { "API client $ClientId" } else { $Username }
    Set-MtConnectionState -Value $state -Account $account -Tenant $baseUri.Host
}

function Test-JamfPro {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Returns $true when the pack has a Jamf Pro token. The tests that need JAMF.JamfPro are skipped otherwise.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()

    $state = Get-MtConnectionState
    [bool]($state -and $state.Token)
}

function Update-JamfProConnection {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Gets a new Jamf Pro token before the current one expires. Maester calls it as the connector's Renew function.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]
    param()

    $state = Get-MtConnectionState
    if ($state -and $PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess($state.Server.Host, 'Get a new Jamf Pro token')) { Update-JamfProToken -State $state }
}

function Disconnect-JamfPro {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Ends the Jamf Pro token and forgets the connection.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param()

    $state = Get-MtConnectionState
    if ($state -and $state.Token) {
        try {
            $null = Invoke-JamfHttp -Uri ([uri]::new($state.Server, 'api/v1/auth/invalidate-token')) -Method POST -TokenRequest `
                -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer $($state.Token)" }
        } catch {
            Write-Verbose "Jamf Pro did not end the token: $($_.Exception.Message)"
        }
    }
    Clear-MtConnectionState
}

function Get-JamfProPagedResult {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Reads every page of a Jamf Pro API list (one that answers with totalCount and results) and returns the results.

    .PARAMETER Path
    The list's path, such as 'api/v3/computer-prestages'.

    .PARAMETER Query
    More query parameters, already encoded, such as 'section=GENERAL&section=SECURITY'.

    .PARAMETER PageSize
    Results per page. Jamf Pro allows up to 2000 on most lists.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([object[]])]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Path,
        [Parameter()] [string] $Query,
        [Parameter()] [ValidateRange(1, 2000)] [int] $PageSize = 500
    )

    $state = Get-MtConnectionState
    $cacheKey = "paged:$Path`?$Query"
    if ($state -and $state.Cache.ContainsKey($cacheKey)) { return , $state.Cache[$cacheKey] }

    $results = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()
    $page = 0
    do {
        $parts = @("page=$page", "page-size=$PageSize")
        if ($Query) { $parts += $Query }
        $response = Invoke-JamfProRequest -Path "$($Path.TrimStart('/'))?$($parts -join '&')" -NoCache
        foreach ($item in @($response.results)) { if ($null -ne $item) { $results.Add($item) } }
        $total = [int]$response.totalCount
        $page++
    } while (@($response.results).Count -gt 0 -and $results.Count -lt $total)

    $array = $results.ToArray()
    if ($state) { $state.Cache[$cacheKey] = $array }
    , $array
}
