## The `[MaesterTest]` attribute

The attribute is read from the file's syntax tree, so its arguments must be constants:

- Named arguments only: `Id = 'CONTOSO.1001'`, never a positional value.
- Values are quoted strings, `$true`, `$false`, or a list in parentheses such as `('T1078.004', 'T1110')`.
- A single string is accepted for a list property: `Service = 'Graph'`.
- A `bool` property can be written as a bare flag: `LongRunning` means `LongRunning = $true`.
- No variables, expressions, `@()` arrays or hashtables.

A value that breaks these rules, an unknown property, or a value outside the allowed list makes the test an
`Error` row with reason `InvalidMetadata`, naming the file and line. The function is never called. If the
message says a property or value "may come from a newer version of Maester", the test was written for a later
release than the one you run.

The attribute answers six questions about a test. Only `Id` and `Title` are required in a custom test; a test
that ships with Maester must also answer the others marked "Built-in tests". The
[attribute rubric](./attribute-rubric.md) says how to choose each value.

| Question | Properties |
| --- | --- |
| Which test is this? | `Id`, `Title` |
| What is it about? | `Product`, `RelatedProduct`, `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType` |
| What do I fix first? | `Severity`, `UserImpact`, `ImplementationCost` |
| What does it map to? | `Mitre`, `Control` |
| Can it run here? | `Service`, `License`, `Permission`, `TenantType`, `Cloud`, `Platform` |
| Is it current? | `Lifecycle`, `ReplacedBy` |

| Property | Type | Allowed values | Required | When omitted | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Id` | string | ID rules above | Always | | Stable identifier. The file is `Test.<Id>.ps1`. Select the test with `-TestId`. |
| `Title` | string | One line | Always | | The title shown in the report. The result row's `Name` is `<Id>: <Title>`. |
| `Product` | string | A product key from the taxonomy (below), or an alias of one. A custom test may use any one line of up to 40 characters | Built-in tests | Empty | The product where the fix is made. Stored and written to the result as the key. The console progress and the run summary group tests by it; tests without one are shown under Other. |
| `RelatedProduct` | string[] | Product keys or aliases; a custom test may use other names | No | None | Other products the test also checks or depends on. Must not repeat `Product`. `-Product` matches them too. |
| `Feature` | string | A feature key of the test's product. A custom test may use any one line of up to 60 characters | Built-in tests | Empty | The part of the product the test is about, for example `conditional-access`. |
| `Area` | string | An area key. A custom test may use any one line of up to 60 characters | Built-in tests | Empty | The security theme, whatever the product, for example `authentication`. |
| `ResourceType` | string | A resource type key such as `Tenant` or `User`. A custom test may use another word of letters and digits | Built-in tests | Empty | What a failing result points at. |
| `Severity` | string | `Critical`, `High`, `Medium`, `Low`, `Info` | Built-in tests | Empty | Default severity. A `TestSettings` row in the config overrides it. |
| `UserImpact` | string | `Low`, `Medium`, `High` | Built-in tests, unless `Severity` is `Info` | Empty | How much the recommended fix disrupts end users. |
| `ImplementationCost` | string | `Low`, `Medium`, `High` | Built-in tests, unless `Severity` is `Info` | Empty | How much administrator work the recommended fix takes. |
| `Mitre` | string[] | MITRE ATT&CK technique IDs (`T1110`, `T1110.003`), or the single value `None` | Built-in tests | None | The techniques the checked control prevents or detects. `None` cannot be combined with an ID. |
| `Control` | string[] | `<framework-key>:<requirement-id>`, for example `cis-m365:5.1.5.1` or `nist-800-53-r5:IA-2(1)` | No | None | The requirements of frameworks the test implements or supports. The first one that a framework file knows becomes the `Benchmark` of the result. See [Mapping a test to a framework](#mapping-a-test-to-a-framework). |
| `Service` | string[] | A name from the service registry (below), or `None` | Built-in tests | No requirement | Services that must **all** be connected. |
| `License` | string[] | Service plan names, not product names; `&` joins plans | No | No requirement | The tenant needs **any one** element. See [License](#license). |
| `Permission` | string[] | `<Service>:<Kind>:<Name>`; `\|` joins alternatives | No | None | The permissions the test needs. The identity needs **every** element, and **any one** alternative inside an element. Recorded on the result row; not enforced in 3.0. See [Permission](#permission). |
| `TenantType` | string[] | `Workforce`, `External` | No | `Workforce` | Tenant types the test applies to. Recorded; enforced only when you turn it on. |
| `Cloud` | string[] | `Commercial`, `GCC`, `GCCHigh`, `DoD`, `China`, `Bleu`, `Delos`, `GovSG` | No | All clouds | Clouds the test applies to. Recorded; enforced only when you turn it on. |
| `Platform` | string[] | `Windows`, `Linux`, `MacOS` | No | All platforms | Operating systems the test can run on. |
| `Lifecycle` | string | `Preview`, `Stable`, `Deprecated` | No | `Stable` | A `Preview` test is not run unless `-IncludePreview`, any `-Tag`, or its exact ID in `-TestId`. A `Deprecated` test still runs; the result row says so. |
| `ReplacedBy` | string | A test ID | No | Empty | The test that took the place of a `Deprecated` test. |
| `LongRunning` | bool | | No | `$false` | Not run unless `-IncludeLongRunning`, `-Tag LongRunning` or `-Tag CAWhatIf`, or its exact ID in `-TestId`. |
| `Exclusive` | bool | | No | `$false` | The test must not run at the same time as another test. Recorded for a future parallel scheduler; no effect in 3.0. |
| `InstanceSource` | string | Name of a function in the same file | No | One result | Makes the test a family with one result per instance. |
| `Tag` | string[] | Non-empty, no commas (spaces allowed) | No | None | Labels of your own for `-Tag` and `-ExcludeTag`. See [Tags](#tags). |
| `Author` | string[] | GitHub handles | Built-in tests | None | Initial authors, credited on maester.dev. |
| `Contributor` | string[] | GitHub handles | No | None | Further contributors, in order of first contribution. |
| `HelpUrl` | string | An `https://` URL | No | The suite's `HelpUrlTemplate` with `{Id}` replaced; none for a custom test without one | The "learn more" link on the result row. |

`Category` and `Preview` were removed in Maester 3.0. A test that still has one is an `Error` row with reason
`InvalidMetadata` and a message that names the replacement: `Product` and `Feature` instead of `Category`, and
`Lifecycle = 'Preview'` instead of `Preview`. The names `OptionalService` and `TimeoutSeconds` are reserved for
later versions and are rejected today.

### Product, feature, area and resource type

The keys come from one registry,
[`powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1`](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1):
the products with their features, the areas and the resource types. Product, feature and area keys are lowercase
kebab-case (`entra`, `conditional-access`, `privileged-access`); resource types are PascalCase (`Tenant`,
`ConditionalAccessPolicy`). The display names live in the registry only.

- A key is matched without regard to case and stored in the registry's spelling. A product can also be named by
  an alias: `Product = 'Entra ID'` loads and is stored as `entra`.
- A test that ships with Maester must use keys from the registry, and a `Feature` that belongs to its
  `Product`. Anything else is `InvalidMetadata`.
- A custom test may use any value. A value that matches the registry is stored as the key; any other value is
  kept as you wrote it.

The result row's `Block`, which 2.x readers and the XML test-case names use, is derived: the display name of
`Product` when the registry knows it, else `Product` as written, else `Feature`, else the `Name` of the folder's
`suite.json`, else `Custom`.

### Tags

`Tag` holds labels that you find useful for your own tests. `-Tag` and `-ExcludeTag` match them, together with
the `Tags` of the folder's `suite.json`. The result row's `Tag` lists the `Tag` values of the test and nothing
else.

Tags are not how Maester classifies a test. Product, feature, area, suite and severity are attributes, and
`Invoke-Maester` selects by them with `-Product`, `-Feature`, `-Area`, `-Suite` and `-Severity`. The tests that
ship with Maester carry no tags for those things. The tags they had in Maester 2.x, such as `CA` or `CIS`, still
select the same tests; see [Selection](../configuration/run-configuration.md#selection).

## The Markdown file

`Test.<ID>.md` has no front matter. It holds:

1. The description: what the test checks and why it matters.
2. A `#### Remediation action` section with the steps to fix a failing result, ideally with a direct link to
   the admin portal page.
3. Optionally `#### Related links`.
4. Exactly one `<!--- Results --->` line followed by `%TestResult%`.

Everything above `<!--- Results --->` becomes the description in the report. The text after it is the result
template: `%TestResult%` is replaced with the `-Result` you pass to `Add-MtTestResultDetail`. The `.md` is also
shown for rows the engine produced without running the test (not selected, skipped because a service is not
connected), so the reader always sees what the test is about.

## What the function returns

| The function does | Result | Reason code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| returns `$true` | `Passed` | |
| returns `$false` | `Failed` | |
| calls `Add-MtTestResultDetail -Investigate` | `Investigate`, whatever it returns | |
| calls `Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause <code>` | `Skipped`. The call ends the test. | `TestSkipped`, or `NotApplicable` for `-SkippedBecause NotApplicable` |
| calls `Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Error`, or throws any error | `Error` | `TestError` |
| returns `$null` without skipping or `-Investigate` | `Skipped` | `NoResult` |
| returns something that is not a boolean, or more than one value | `Error` | `InvalidReturn` |
| runs longer than the configured timeout | `Error` | `Timeout` |

When several apply, they are evaluated in this order: `-SkippedBecause Error`, `-Investigate`, any other
skip, an uncaught error, the returned value.

Watch for stray output. A command whose output you do not capture (`$list.Add($x)` on an `ArrayList`, for
example) adds a second value to the function's output and turns the result into `InvalidReturn`. Assign such
calls to `$null` or pipe them to `Out-Null`.

### Add-MtTestResultDetail

[`Add-MtTestResultDetail`](../commands/Add-MtTestResultDetail.mdx) works as in 2.x. The parameters you use in a
native test:

- `-Result`: the Markdown result. It replaces `%TestResult%` in the `.md` file.
- `-GraphObjects` and `-GraphObjectType`: a list of objects rendered as a table with links to the admin
  portal, inserted where `%TestResult%` appears in `-Result`. See
  [Formatting test results](./formatting-test-results.md).
- `-Investigate`: the result needs a person to look at it.
- `-SkippedBecause`: skip the test for a reason only the test can see, such as `NotApplicable`,
  `NotSupportedAppPermission` or `Custom` with `-SkippedCustomReason`. Do not use the `NotConnected*` and
  `NotLicensed*` codes for conditions the attribute can declare; use `Service` and `License`.
- `-Description`: replaces the description from the `.md` file. Leave it out to use the `.md`.

`-TestTitle` and `-Severity` are ignored in a single-result native test: the title and severity come from the
attribute and the config. In a family, `-TestTitle` sets the instance's title when the instance object has no
`Title`. `-Severity` is used only when neither the config nor the attribute sets one.

### Embedding another tool's report

A test or a family's instance source that runs another tool can embed that tool's own single-file HTML report in
the Maester report with `Add-MtReportAttachment`:

```powershell
Add-MtReportAttachment -Name 'Zero Trust Assessment' -Path "$outputPath/ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html"
```

The report lists it near the bottom of the left menu (a pack's test's report goes in that pack's menu instead), and shows a button with that name on its overview page and
on the test's result (on every instance of a family). Each opens the embedded report in the main panel, beside the
Maester navigation, with a link to open it in a new browser tab. The attached report runs in a sandboxed frame
without access to the Maester report or its data. It works offline, so the Maester report stays one
file to share. The file is read and compressed at once, so you can delete the tool's output folder afterwards. The JSON
results file lists the attachment's name and size, not its content, and the HTML report leaves HTML attachments out
when `-RedactUserIdentity` is used.

With `-ContentType application/json`, an attachment is data for a view built into the report, which finds it by
its `Name` (the Zero Trust Assessment pack attaches its Zero Trust plan as `zero-trust-workshop`). It is not shown
as a button, and under `-RedactUserIdentity` it is redacted like the results instead of being left out.

### Errors and skips

Do not wrap the body in `try`/`catch` only to report `-SkippedBecause Error`. The engine runs every test inside
its own `try`, so any terminating error ends the test and becomes an `Error` row with the exception message as
`ReasonDetail` and the error record in `ErrorRecord`. Statement-terminating errors (a failed command, a method
call on `$null`) also end the test, so it cannot carry on with empty data and return `$true` by accident.

You may still use `try`/`catch` for a condition you handle, for example a 403 from Graph that you report as
`-SkippedBecause NotAuthorized`. A `-SkippedBecause` call made inside your own `try` block still skips the
test; the engine recognises the skip when your `catch` passes it to `Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause
Error -SkippedError $_`.

Warnings and non-terminating errors written by the test are shown on the console and stored on the result row
in `Diagnostics`.

## Declare what the test needs

Do not check connections or licences in the test. Declare them, and the engine decides before the test runs.
## Parameters

A test's `param()` block lists the values a user can tune per tenant: thresholds, switches, objects to exclude.
Values come from the run configuration or from `Invoke-MtTest -Parameter`; a test always has to run with none
set, using its defaults.

```powershell
param(
    # Longest validity period, in days, that a certificate may be issued for.
    [ValidateRange(1, 3650)]
    [int] $MaximumValidityDays = 365,

    # Members of these groups are exempt from this check.
    [MaesterParameter(Kind = 'Entra.Group')]
    [string[]] $ExcludedGroups,

    # How strictly to evaluate.
    [ValidateSet('Strict', 'Lenient')]
    [string] $Mode = 'Strict'
)
```

Rules:

- Types are `int`, `bool`, `switch`, `string` or `string[]`.
- Defaults are constants. No parameter is mandatory.
- Every parameter has a description: a `#` comment on the line directly above it, or `.PARAMETER` help. Only
  the comment line nearest the parameter is read, so keep the comment to one line or use `.PARAMETER`.
  `Get-MtTest` shows the description.
- Give thresholds a `ValidateRange`. A `ValidateSet` makes the parameter a list of choices.
- `Instance` and every name that starts with `Mt` belong to the engine and cannot be set.

Set values in the config:

```json
{
  "TestSettings": [
    { "Id": "CONTOSO.1002", "Parameters": { "ReasonMarker": "Off:" } },
    { "Id": "MT.1198", "Parameters": { "MaximumValidityDays": 180 } }
  ]
}
```

The engine checks each value against the `param()` block before the test runs. A name the test does not have,
a fraction for an `int`, a number for a `string`, a string for a `bool` or `switch`, or a value outside the
`ValidateRange` or `ValidateSet` gives that test an `Error` row with reason `InvalidConfiguration`; the run
carries on. A `string[]` parameter accepts one string or a list. The effective values, and where each came from
(`Default`, `Config` or `Parameter`), are written to the result row's `Parameters`.

### Parameter kinds

`[MaesterParameter(Kind = '...')]` says what a string parameter holds, so a user interface can offer a picker
and the engine can check the value's shape:

| Kind | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `Entra.User` | User object ID |
| `Entra.Group` | Group object ID |
| `Entra.ServicePrincipal` | Service principal object ID |
| `Entra.Application` | Application object ID |
| `Entra.ConditionalAccessPolicy` | Conditional Access policy ID |
| `Entra.NamedLocation` | Named location ID |
| `Entra.Domain` | Domain name |
| `Entra.DirectoryRole` | Directory role definition ID |
| `Azure.Subscription` | Subscription ID |
| `Azure.ResourceGroup` | Resource group ID (`/subscriptions/<id>/resourceGroups/<name>`) |
| `Azure.Resource` | Azure resource ID |

config a value can be the ID itself or an object `{ "Id": "...", "DisplayName": "..." }`; the test always
receives the ID.

  A mobile device is a computing device that has a small form factor such that it can easily be carried by a single individual; is designed to operate without a physical connection; possesses local, non-removable or removable data storage; and includes a self-contained power source. Mobile device functionality may also include voice communication capabilities, on-board sensors that allow the device to capture information, and/or built-in features for synchronizing local data with remote locations. Examples include smart phones and tablets. Mobile devices are typically associated with a single individual. The processing, storage, and transmission capability of the mobile device may be comparable to or merely a subset of notebook/desktop systems, depending on the nature and intended purpose of the device. Protection and control of mobile devices is behavior or policy-based and requires users to take physical action to protect and control such devices when outside of controlled areas. Controlled areas are spaces for which organizations provide physical or procedural controls to meet the requirements established for protecting information and systems.

  Due to the large variety of mobile devices with different characteristics and capabilities, organizational restrictions may vary for the different classes or types of such devices. Usage restrictions and specific implementation guidance for mobile devices include configuration management, device identification and authentication, implementation of mandatory protective software, scanning devices for malicious code, updating virus protection software, scanning for critical software updates and patches, conducting primary operating system (and possibly other resident software) integrity checks, and disabling unnecessary hardware.

input.content:
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Writes tests/frameworks/mscp.json, the catalogue of the NIST macOS Security Compliance Project (mSCP) rules, from a
checkout of usnistgov/macos_security.

.DESCRIPTION
The fleet compliance results of Jamf Pro's Compliance Benchmarks name each rule by its mSCP rule ID, such as
os_gatekeeper_enable. This catalogue lets Maester show each result under its rule, with the rule's CIS macOS, DISA
STIG, NIST SP 800-53, NIST SP 800-171 and CMMC references.

Only identifiers and facts are written: the rule ID, its section, the mSCP baselines it is in and its references.
No rule text is copied. mSCP is licensed CC BY 4.0 (Apple's vendor description text excluded); the pack's README
gives the attribution.

Needs the powershell-yaml module: Install-PSResource powershell-yaml.

.PARAMETER MscpPath
A checkout of https://github.com/usnistgov/macos_security.

.PARAMETER MacOSVersion
The macOS major version whose CIS benchmark and DISA STIG references are written as Related references.

.EXAMPLE
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/usnistgov/macos_security ../macos_security
./build/Update-MscpFramework.ps1 -MscpPath ../macos_security
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $MscpPath,
    [Parameter()] [ValidatePattern('^\d{2}$')] [string] $MacOSVersion = '26'
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
Import-Module powershell-yaml

$root = (Resolve-Path $MscpPath).Path
$rulesPath = Join-Path $root 'rules'
if (-not (Test-Path $rulesPath)) { throw "$MscpPath has no rules folder. Point -MscpPath at a checkout of usnistgov/macos_security." }

# The release, for the framework's version: the newest heading of the changelog, such as "mSCP 2.0 Release 27.1".
$version = $null
$changelog = Join-Path $root 'CHANGELOG.md'
if (Test-Path $changelog) {
    $heading = Select-String -LiteralPath $changelog -Pattern '^#+\s*\[?([^\]\r\n]*Release[^\]\r\n]*|v?\d+\.\d+[^\]\r\n]*)' | Select-Object -First 1
    if ($heading) { $version = $heading.Matches[0].Groups[1].Value.Trim() }
}
if (-not $version) { $version = (git -C $root describe --tags --always 2>$null) }
if (-not $version) { throw 'Could not read the mSCP release from CHANGELOG.md or git.' }

# The baselines each rule is in, from the macOS baselines of this macOS version.
$baselineOf = @{}
$baselineFiles = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath (Join-Path $root 'baselines/macos') -Filter "*_macos_$MacOSVersion.0.yaml" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
foreach ($file in $baselineFiles) {
    $name = $file.BaseName -replace "_macos_$MacOSVersion\.0$", ''
    if ($name -eq 'all_rules') { continue }
    $baseline = Get-Content -LiteralPath $file.FullName -Raw | ConvertFrom-Yaml
    foreach ($section in $baseline.profile) {
        foreach ($rule in $section.rules) {
            if (-not $baselineOf.ContainsKey($rule)) { $baselineOf[$rule] = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new() }
            $baselineOf[$rule].Add($name)
        }
    }
}
if ($baselineOf.Count -eq 0) { throw "No macOS $MacOSVersion baselines in $root/baselines/macos. Pick another -MacOSVersion." }

$requirements = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()
$files = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $rulesPath -Filter '*.yaml' -Recurse -FollowSymlink
foreach ($file in ($files | Sort-Object Name)) {
    $rule = Get-Content -LiteralPath $file.FullName -Raw | ConvertFrom-Yaml
    if (-not $rule.id -or -not $rule.platforms -or -not $rule.platforms.ContainsKey('macOS')) { continue }
    $refs = $rule.references
    $related = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
    foreach ($c in @($refs.nist.'800-53r5')) { if ($c -and $c -ne 'N/A') { $related.Add("nist-800-53-r5:$c") } }
    foreach ($c in @($refs.nist.'800-171r3')) { if ($c -and $c -ne 'N/A') { $related.Add("nist-800-171-r3:$c") } }
    foreach ($c in @($refs.disa.cmmc)) { if ($c -and $c -ne 'N/A') { $related.Add("cmmc-2:$c") } }
    $cisLevel = $null
    foreach ($c in @($refs.cis.benchmark."macos_$MacOSVersion")) {
        if ($c -match '^\s*([\d.]+)\s*(\(level (\d)\))?') {
            $related.Add("cis-apple-macos-$($MacOSVersion):$($Matches[1])")
            if ($Matches[3]) { $cisLevel = "L$($Matches[3])" }
        }
    }
    foreach ($c in @($refs.disa.disa_stig."macos_$MacOSVersion")) { if ($c -and $c -ne 'N/A') { $related.Add("disa-apple-macos-$MacOSVersion-stig:$c") } }
    foreach ($c in @($refs.cis.controls_v8)) { if ($c -and $c -ne 'N/A') { $related.Add("cis-controls-v8:$c") } }

    $requirement = [ordered]@{ Id = [string]$rule.id; Section = $file.Directory.Name }
    if ($baselineOf.ContainsKey($rule.id)) { $requirement.Baselines = @($baselineOf[$rule.id] | Sort-Object -Unique) }
    if ($cisLevel) { $requirement.CisLevel = $cisLevel }
    if ($related.Count) { $requirement.Related = @($related | Select-Object -Unique) }
    $requirements.Add($requirement)
}

$framework = [ordered]@{
    Framework    = 'mscp'
    Name         = 'NIST macOS Security Compliance Project'
    Version      = $version
    Url          = 'https://github.com/usnistgov/macos_security'
    License      = 'CC BY 4.0. Includes contributions from the US Government, the public and Apple Inc.'
    Requirements = $requirements
}
$out = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '../tests/frameworks/mscp.json'
$null = New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path (Split-Path $out) -Force
$framework | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6 | Set-Content -LiteralPath $out -Encoding utf8NoBOM
Write-Host "Wrote $($requirements.Count) macOS rules of mSCP $version to $out."

58	All paths are relative to `https://{region}.api.jamfcloud.com/compliance-benchmarks`, and every one requires `X-Environment-Id`. Source: cbe.json `paths`, `responses` and `components.schemas`.
59	
60	| Method and path | operationId | Scope | Responses declared |
61	|---|---|---|---|
62	| `GET /v1/baselines` | getBaselines | read | 200, 401, 403 |
63	| `GET /v1/rules?baseline-id={id}` | getRules | read¹ | 200, 400 |
64	| `GET /v1/benchmarks` | getTenantBenchmarks | read | 200, 401, 403 |
65	| `GET /v1/benchmarks/{id}` | getBenchmark | read | 200, 400, 401, 403, 404 |
66	| `GET /v1/benchmarks/{id}/rules` | v1GetBenchmarkRulesStats | read | 200, 400 |
67	| `GET /v1/benchmarks/{id}/devices?rule-id=…` | v1GetDevicesForBenchmarkRule | read | 200, 400 |
68	| `GET /v1/benchmarks/{id}/compliance-percentage` | v1GetBenchmarkCompliancePercentage | read | 200, 400, 404 |
69	| `POST /v1/benchmarks` | postBenchmark | create | 202, 400, 401, 403, 409. **Never call this.** |
70	| `DELETE /v1/benchmarks/{id}` | deleteBenchmark | delete | 204, 400, 401, 403. **Never call this.** |
71	
72	¹ The description of `getRules` names no permission, but its `security` block requires `compliance-benchmarks:read`. The spec's parameter is `baseline-id`. The permissions map writes "`/rules?baselineId=`". **Which spelling the live API accepts is UNVERIFIED**; the spec's `baseline-id` is the likelier one.
73	
74	Several operations do not declare 401 or 403 in the spec, but the gateway can still return them. Handle them for every call.
75	
76	### 2.1 `GET /v1/baselines`
77	- Returns `BaselinesResponse`, which is `{baselines: [BaselineInfo]}`.
78	- `BaselineInfo` has `id`, `baselineId`, `title`, `description` and `ruleCount`, all required.
79	- The description reads "Returns list of the mSCP baselines allowed for the Compliance benchmarks".
80	
81	### 2.2 `GET /v1/rules?baseline-id=…`
82	- Returns `SourcedRules`, which is `{availableOsVersions, rules: [RuleInfo], sources}`. All three are required.
83	- The `Source` type (`branch`, `revision`) is marked `deprecated: true`.
84	- `RuleInfo` has these fields; the required ones are `id`, `title`, `description`, `enabled`, `sectionName`, `supportedOs` and `osSpecificDefaults`:
85	  - `id`, `title`, `description`, `enabled`, `sectionName`
86	  - `supportedOs`, an array of `OsInfo`: `osType` (`MAC_OS`, `IOS` or `VISION_OS`), `osVersion` (an integer) and `managementType` (`MANAGED` or `BYOD`)
87	  - `osSpecificDefaults`, an object of `{title, description, odv: {value, hint}}`
88	  - `odv`, an `OrganizationDefinedValue`: `type` (`INTEGER`, `STRING`, `ENUM`, `REGEX` or `BOOLEAN`), `value`, `placeholder`, `hint` and `validation` (`enumValues`, `min`, `max`, `regex`)
89	  - `references`, a nullable string array
90	  - `reportable`, `smartCard`
91	  - `ruleRelation`: `dependsOn`, `conflictsWith` and `defaultDisabled` (required)
92	
93	### 2.3 `GET /v1/benchmarks`
94	- Returns `BenchmarksResponseV2`, which is `{benchmarks: [BenchmarkV2]}`. It has no pagination parameters.
95	- `BenchmarkV2` has `id`, `title`, `description`, `syncState`, `target.deviceGroups[]`, `modified` and `updateAvailable`, all required.
96	- `syncState` is one of `SYNCED`, `PENDING`, `FAILED`, `DELETING` or `DELETE_FAILED`.
97	
98	### 2.4 `GET /v1/benchmarks/{id}`
99	- Returns `BenchmarkResponseV2`. Its required fields:
100	  - `benchmarkId`, `tenantId`, `title`, `description`
101	  - `baselineId`
102	  - `enforcementMode` (`MONITOR` or `MONITOR_AND_ENFORCE`)
103	  - `canSwitchToEnforce`, `deleted`, `lastUpdatedAt`
104	  - `rules` (`[RuleInfo]`)
105	  - `availableOsVersions`, `selectedOsVersions`, `target`, `updateAvailable`
106	  - `sources`, which is marked deprecated
107	- The description says it returns a 404 if the benchmark is not found.
108	
109	### 2.5 `GET /v1/benchmarks/{id}/rules`
110	- Query parameters:
111	  - `rule-search`
112	  - `page` (default 0)
113	  - `page-size` (default **500**)
114	  - `sort` (default `ruleNumber,ruleTitle`)
115	- Returns `{totalCount, results: [RuleResult]}`.
116	- `RuleResult` requires `ruleId`, `ruleTitle`, `passed`, `failed`, `unknown`, `passPercentage` and `numberOfDevices`.
117	- Optional fields:
118	  - `ruleNumber`: "Rule number in the benchmark, if applicable. E.g. CIS numbers like '2.5.1.1'."
119	  - `sectionName`: "mSCP category the rule belongs to, e.g. 'Passcode' or 'Auditing'."
120	  - `discussion`
121	
122	### 2.6 `GET /v1/benchmarks/{id}/devices`
123	- Query parameters:
124	  - `rule-id`
125	  - `device-search`
126	  - `rule-result` (`PASSED`, `FAILED` or `UNKNOWN`)
127	  - `page` (default 0)
128	  - `page-size` (default **100**)
129	  - `sort` (default `ruleResult:desc`)
130	- Returns `{totalCount, results: [DeviceRuleResult]}`. Each result has `deviceId`, `deviceName` (nullable) and `state`; `deviceId` and `state` are required.
131	- `deviceId` is described as "Device Platform ID", not the Jamf Pro computer ID.
132	
133	### 2.7 `GET /v1/benchmarks/{id}/compliance-percentage`
134	- Returns `{compliancePercentage: number}`.
135	- The description gives the calculation as "sum of device compliance scores divided by number of devices".
136	- A 404 means "Benchmark has no applicable rules for reporting calculations". Treat it as "no data", not as an error.
137	
138	**Pagination and errors.**
139	- This API has no `filter` parameter.
140	- `ApiError` is `{httpStatus, traceId, errors[]}`, all required.

144	## 3. Requirements and limits
145	
146	Source: https://learn.jamf.com/r/en-US/jamf-compliance-benchmarks-configuration-guide/Compliance_Benchmarks_Requirements. I re-fetched it on 2026-11-09.

148	- **Hosting:** "Jamf Commercial Cloud, Jamf Premium Cloud, or Jamf High Compliance Cloud-hosted environment". It is "Not available for Jamf GovCloud Premium Cloud Plus". The page does not mention on-premises, and the gateway serves only cloud regions. So **on-premises is not supported**: this is an inference from those two facts, and the page never says it outright.
149	- **Jamf Pro version:** "Jamf Pro 11.16.0 or later".
150	- **Operating system:** "Computers with macOS 15 or later". The page does not mention iOS or visionOS. The API's enums include `IOS` and `VISION_OS`, but **support for them is UNVERIFIED**.
151	- **Sign-in:** "OIDC authentication enabled in Jamf Pro". The note adds that you must then log in with a Jamf ID or IdP credentials.

163	## 4. Rule identifiers and cross-references
164	
165	- **Rule IDs are mSCP rule IDs.**
166	  - The examples in cbe.json are mSCP IDs such as `os_install_log_retention_configure` and `supplemental_password_policy`.
167	  - `/v1/baselines` is described as returning mSCP baselines.
168	  - So `ruleId` can be joined to the mSCP YAML `id`.
169	- **Cross-references in the API are limited.**
170	  - `RuleResult.ruleNumber` carries a benchmark number, such as a CIS number.
171	  - `RuleInfo.references` is a nullable string array. Its meaning is not documented. **What it holds for non-CIS baselines is UNVERIFIED.**
172	  - No STIG ID, NIST control or CCI field is documented. Join to mSCP to get them.

177	
178	- **Latest release:** "mSCP 2.0, Release 27.1", tag `release_27.1`, published 2026-10-22T16:51:53Z, targeting `main`.
179	  - The release before it is "mSCP 2.0, Release 27.0", 2026-09-11.

228	## 6. Fallback: reading on-device results through Jamf Pro inventory
229	
230	### mSCP compliance script
231	I verified this against `cs.jinja`, which is https://github.com/usnistgov/macos_security/blob/release_27.1/src/mscp/data/templates/shell_scripts/compliance_script.sh.jinja.
232	- **Results plist:** `/Library/Preferences/org.<baseline>.audit.plist` (line 86). Each rule has a `finding` key, where `true` means the rule failed. `lastComplianceCheck` and `computerName` are written at lines 337–338.
233	- **Log and CSV:** `/Library/Logs/<hostname>_<baseline>_baseline.log` and `.csv` (lines 87–88). The CSV header is `Rule,Status,Result,Expected,Exemption` (line 139).
234	- **Exemptions:** `exempt` and `exempt_reason` are read through the `org.<baseline>.audit` preference domain (lines 246 and 307), so a managed profile can set them.
235	- **Counts:** `compliance_count` counts an exempt failed rule as both non-compliant and exempt (lines 233–264).
236	- **Flags:** the usage text lists `--check`, `--fix`, `--cfc`, `--stats`, `--compliant`, `--non_compliant`, `--reset`, `--reset-all` and `--quiet=` (line 417). JSON output exists (`print_json`, line 350, which pipes to `jq`), but `--json` is not in the usage text. **Its exact flag spelling is UNVERIFIED.**
237	
238	### Extension attributes
239	1. **Jamf Compliance Benchmarks feature.** "An extension attribute titled "[Benchmark Name] - Failed Result List" is automatically created for each benchmark." The documented compliance check is a smart group "that checks if the failed result list is empty" (https://learn.jamf.com/r/en-US/jamf-compliance-benchmarks-configuration-guide/Compliance_Benchmarks_and_Third-Party_Compliance_Workflows, re-fetched). The page does not document the format of the value, so it is **UNVERIFIED**.
240	2. **JCE.** JCE creates four EAs: "Compliance - Exemptions", "Compliance - Failed Result List", "Compliance - Failed Results Count" and "Compliance - Version". Source: JCE User Guide v1.5.0, September 2025, p. 26, with the EA descriptions on p. 36 (`txt/guide.txt`, lines 480–500 and 680–700); https://github.com/Jamf-Concepts/jamf-compliance-editor.
241	   - Failed Results Count excludes exempt rules. For example, five failures with two exemptions gives 3.
242	   - Failed Result List includes exempt rules.
243	   - Exemptions come from `/Library/Managed Preferences/org.<baseline>.audit.plist`.
244	   - JCE 1.2 and later lets the admin choose what to upload, so these EAs may be missing.
245	3. **Community variants.** These are https://github.com/jordanburnette/mSCP_EAs and a blog post at https://tonyyo11.github.io/posts/Generating-Monthly-Trend-Reports-mSCP. I did not re-check either; they are not primary sources. Match EA names by pattern, for example `Failed Result(s)? (List|Count)`.
246	
247	### Reading the EAs through the Jamf Pro API
248	I verified this against pro.json (version 11.33.0, the gateway copy at server `https://{region}.api.jamfcloud.com/pro`). On a Jamf Pro server the same paths sit under `{server}/api`.
249	- **Use `GET /api/v4/computers-inventory?section=EXTENSION_ATTRIBUTES&page=0&page-size=100`.**
250	  - `/v3/computers-inventory` is **deprecated**: "As of 2026-07-14, this endpoint has been deprecated and will be removed in a future release" (`x-deprecation-date: 2026-07-14`).
251	  - Both versions take `section` (default `GENERAL`), `page`, `page-size`, `sort` (default `general.name:asc`) and `filter`.
252	  - `EXTENSION_ATTRIBUTES` is a value in both `ComputerSectionV3` and `ComputerSectionV4`.
253	  - The fields of `ComputerExtensionAttribute` are `definitionId`, `name`, `values`, `dataType`, `description`, `enabled`, `inputType`, `multiValue` and `options`.
254	  - Older servers have only v1 or v3. **The Jamf Pro version that introduced v4 or v3 is UNVERIFIED.** The connector should fall back from v4 to v3 to v1.
255	- **`GET /api/v1/computer-extension-attributes`** lists the EA definitions. It takes `page`, `page-size`, `sort` (default `name.asc`) and `filter`.
256	- **Privileges** for a read-only Jamf Pro API role, now verified from pro.json `x-required-privileges-legacy`:
257	  - **"Read Computers"** for computers-inventory. The gateway scope is `devices:read`.
258	  - **"Read Computer Extension Attributes"** for computer-extension-attributes. The gateway scope is `extension-attributes:read`.

260	### Does the Jamf Pro API expose benchmark results?
261	No.
262	- pro.json 11.33.0 has no benchmark or mSCP paths. Its only compliance paths are `/v1/conditional-access/device-compliance-information/{computer|mobile}/{deviceId}` (privilege `device-compliance-information:read`) and `/v1/conditional-access/device-compliance/feature-toggle` (`conditional-access:read`).
263	- The permissions map places Compliance Benchmarks under the Platform API: "`/benchmarks`, `/benchmarks/{id}`, `/benchmarks/{id}/rules`, `/{id}/devices`, `/{id}/compliance-percentage`" and "`/baselines`, `/rules?baselineId=`".
264	- It also lists "macOS compliance baselines (Protect `listBaselineRules`)" as **Deprecated**.
265	- I did not check the Classic API for compliance endpoints, so their absence there is **UNVERIFIED**.

269	## Summary for the connector design
270	- **Primary route (cloud only):** a Jamf Account integration at environment scope with `compliance-benchmarks:read`.
271	  1. Get a token from `https://{region}.api.jamfcloud.com/auth/token` and renew it before 900 seconds.
272	  2. Call `GET /compliance-benchmarks/v1/benchmarks`.
273	  3. For each benchmark, call `/v1/benchmarks/{id}` (for `baselineId` and `enforcementMode`), `/compliance-percentage` (where a 404 means no data) and `/rules?page-size=500` (paging while `totalCount` exceeds the results returned).
274	  4. Optionally call `/devices?rule-id=…&rule-result=FAILED`.
275	  5. Send `X-Environment-Id` on every call and back off on any `429`.
276	- **Fallback (cloud and on-premises):** use the Jamf Pro API client with "Read Computers" and "Read Computer Extension Attributes".
277	  - Read `GET /api/v4/computers-inventory?section=EXTENSION_ATTRIBUTES`, falling back to v3 or v1.
278	  - Match these EA names by pattern: "[Benchmark] - Failed Result List", "Compliance - Failed Results Count" and "Failed Result List".
279	- **Crosswalk:** join `ruleId` to the mSCP `release_27.1` YAML. Handle both the 2.0 and the legacy formats.
280

283	- iOS and visionOS support
284	- what `RuleInfo.references` holds
285	- the value format of the benchmark EA
286	- the Jamf Pro version that introduced v3 and v4 computers-inventory
287	- the exact JSON flag of the compliance script
288	- whether the Classic API has compliance endpoints

<#
.SYNOPSIS
Writes tests/frameworks/disa-jamf-pro-stig.json, the catalogue of the DISA Jamf Pro v10.x EMM STIG, from DISA's
XCCDF file.

.DESCRIPTION
The tenant checks of the pack name the STIG rule they support in Control, such as
disa-jamf-pro-stig:V-241798. This catalogue gives Maester each rule's severity (CAT I to III), STIG ID and rule ID,
and its CCIs as Related references.

STIGs are works of the US Government and in the public domain. Download the STIG zip from
https://public.cyber.mil/stigs/downloads/ (search for Jamf), unzip it and pass the Manual-xccdf.xml file.

.PARAMETER XccdfPath
The U_Jamf_Pro_v10-x_EMM_STIG_V<n>R<n>_Manual-xccdf.xml file.

.EXAMPLE
./build/Update-JamfStigFramework.ps1 -XccdfPath ./REDACTED.xml
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $XccdfPath)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
[xml]$xml = Get-Content -LiteralPath $XccdfPath -Raw
$ns = [System.Xml.XmlNamespaceManager]::new($xml.NameTable)
$ns.AddNamespace('x', 'http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.1')
$benchmark = $xml.SelectSingleNode('/x:Benchmark', $ns)
if (-not $benchmark) { throw "$XccdfPath is not an XCCDF 1.1 benchmark." }

$release = $benchmark.SelectSingleNode("x:plain-text[@id='release-info']", $ns).InnerText
if ($release -notmatch 'Release:\s*(\d+)') { throw "Could not read the release from '$release'." }
$version = "V$($benchmark.SelectSingleNode('x:version', $ns).InnerText)R$($Matches[1])"
$date = if ($release -match 'Benchmark Date:\s*(.+)$') { $Matches[1].Trim() }

$category = @{ high = 'CAT I'; medium = 'CAT II'; low = 'CAT III' }
$requirements = foreach ($group in $benchmark.SelectNodes('x:Group', $ns)) {
    $rule = $group.SelectSingleNode('x:Rule', $ns)
    $ccis = @($rule.SelectNodes("x:ident[@system='http://cyber.mil/cci']", $ns) | ForEach-Object { "cci:$($_.InnerText)" })
    $requirement = [ordered]@{
        Id       = $group.id
        StigId   = $rule.SelectSingleNode('x:version', $ns).InnerText
        RuleId   = $rule.id
        Severity = $category[[string]$rule.severity]
    }
    if ($ccis) { $requirement.Related = $ccis }
    $requirement
}

$framework = [ordered]@{
    Framework    = 'disa-jamf-pro-stig'
    Name         = 'DISA Jamf Pro v10.x EMM STIG'
    Version      = $version
    Date         = $date
    Url          = 'https://public.cyber.mil/stigs/downloads/'
    Requirements = @($requirements)
}
$out = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '../tests/frameworks/disa-jamf-pro-stig.json'
$null = New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path (Split-Path $out) -Force
$framework | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5 | Set-Content -LiteralPath $out -Encoding utf8NoBOM
Write-Host "Wrote $(@($requirements).Count) rules of the Jamf Pro STIG $version ($date) to $out."

function Measure-JamfDevice {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Counts the devices that meet a condition, and writes the result of a fleet check.

    .DESCRIPTION
    The fleet checks all have the same shape: of the devices the check applies to, what share meets the
    requirement, against the lowest share the test accepts. This writes the Markdown result (the counts and a table
    of up to MaximumListed devices that do not meet it) and returns $true when the share is high enough.

    Skips the test when no device applies, with -NoDeviceReason.

    .PARAMETER Device
    The devices the check applies to.

    .PARAMETER Condition
    A script block that gets one device as $_ and returns $true when it meets the requirement.

    .PARAMETER Describe
    A script block that gets one device that fails as $_ and returns an ordered hashtable of the columns to show.

    .PARAMETER MinimumPercent
    The lowest share of devices, in percent, that must meet the requirement.

    .PARAMETER Requirement
    The requirement in a few words, such as "have FileVault on".

    .PARAMETER Noun
    The kind of device, such as Macs.

    .PARAMETER NoDeviceReason
    Why the test is skipped when no device applies.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [AllowEmptyCollection()] [object[]] $Device,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [scriptblock] $Condition,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [scriptblock] $Describe,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [int] $MinimumPercent,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Requirement,
        [Parameter()] [string] $Noun = 'Macs',
        [Parameter()] [string] $NoDeviceReason = 'Jamf Pro manages no device this check applies to.',
        [Parameter()] [int] $MaximumListed = 50
    )

    if ($Device.Count -eq 0) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason $NoDeviceReason
        return
    }

    $failing = @($Device | Where-Object { -not (& $Condition) })
    $meeting = $Device.Count - $failing.Count
    $percent = [math]::Floor(100 * $meeting / $Device.Count * 10) / 10
    $passed = $percent -ge $MinimumPercent

    $summary = "$meeting of $($Device.Count) $Noun ($percent%) $Requirement. The test needs at least $MinimumPercent%."
    $result = if ($passed -and $failing.Count -eq 0) { "Well done. All $($Device.Count) $Noun $Requirement." }
    elseif ($passed) { "Well done. $summary" }
    else { $summary }

    if ($failing.Count -gt 0) {
        $rows = @($failing | Select-Object -First $MaximumListed | ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject](& $Describe) })
        $result += "`n`n$(ConvertTo-JamfMarkdownTable -InputObject $rows)"
        if ($failing.Count -gt $MaximumListed) { $result += "`n`nAnd $($failing.Count - $MaximumListed) more." }
    }
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $result
    $passed
}

function Connect-JamfPlatform {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Connects the pack to the Jamf Platform API, which serves the results of Jamf Pro's Compliance Benchmarks.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Connect-Maester -Service JAMF.Platform calls this. Its parameters come from -ServiceSetting, from
    Connections.JAMF.Platform in maester-config.json, or from MAESTER_JAMF_PLATFORM_<NAME> environment variables.

    The Platform API uses its own credentials, not the Jamf Pro API client: an integration in Jamf Account, scoped
    to the Jamf Pro environment, with only the compliance-benchmarks:read scope. Its environment ID is shown in the
    integration's details in Jamf Account. Compliance Benchmarks needs Jamf Cloud and Jamf Pro 11.16 or later.

    .PARAMETER Region
    The region of the Jamf Cloud instance: us, eu or apac.

    .PARAMETER ClientId
    The client ID of the Jamf Account integration.

    .PARAMETER ClientSecret
    The client secret of the integration. Prefer the MAESTER_JAMF_PLATFORM_CLIENTSECRET environment variable.

    .PARAMETER EnvironmentId
    The ID of the Jamf Pro environment, a GUID.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [ValidateSet('us', 'eu', 'apac')] [string] $Region,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $ClientId,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $ClientSecret,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [ValidatePattern('^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-([0-9a-fA-F]{4}-){3}[0-9a-fA-F]{12}$')] [string] $EnvironmentId
    )

    $state = @{
        Server        = [uri]"https://$($Region.ToLowerInvariant()).api.jamfcloud.com/"
        ClientId      = $ClientId
        ClientSecret  = REDACTED
        EnvironmentId = $EnvironmentId
        Cache         = @{}
    }
    Update-JamfPlatformToken -State $state
    Set-MtConnectionState -Service 'JAMF.Platform' -Value $state -Account "Jamf Account integration $ClientId" -Tenant "Jamf environment $EnvironmentId ($Region)"
}

function Test-JamfPlatform {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Returns $true when the pack has a Jamf Platform API token. The tests that need JAMF.Platform do not run otherwise.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()

    $state = Get-MtConnectionState -Service 'JAMF.Platform'
    [bool]($state -and $state.Token)
}

function Update-JamfPlatformConnection {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Gets a new Platform API token before the current one expires. Maester calls it as the connector's Renew function.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]
    param()

    $state = Get-MtConnectionState -Service 'JAMF.Platform'
    if ($state -and $PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess($state.Server.Host, 'Get a new Jamf Platform API token')) { Update-JamfPlatformToken -State $state }
}

function Disconnect-JamfPlatform {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Forgets the Platform API connection. Its token expires on its own after 15 minutes.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param()

    Clear-MtConnectionState -Service 'JAMF.Platform'
}

function Test-MPJAMF1018 {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that FileVault encrypts the startup disk of the Macs that Jamf Pro manages.
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id                 = 'MP.JAMF.1018',
        Title              = 'FileVault encrypts managed Macs',
        Product            = 'Jamf Pro',
        Feature            = 'Disk encryption',
        Area               = 'data-protection',
        ResourceType       = 'Device',
        Severity           = 'High',
        UserImpact         = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
        Mitre              = ('T1005', 'T1025'),
        Control            = ('mscp:system_settings_filevault_enforce', 'nist-800-53-r5:SC-28'),
        Service            = 'JAMF.JamfPro',
        Author             = 'merill'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # Lowest share of managed Macs, in percent, that must have FileVault on.
        [ValidateRange(1, 100)]
        [int] $MinimumPercent = 95
    )

    # Macs that cannot report FileVault (NOT_APPLICABLE) are left out.
    $macs = @(Get-JamfProComputer | Where-Object { [string]$_.operatingSystem.fileVault2Status -ne 'NOT_APPLICABLE' })

    $measure = @{
        Device         = $macs
        Condition      = { [string]$_.operatingSystem.fileVault2Status -in 'ALL_ENCRYPTED', 'BOOT_ENCRYPTED' }
        Describe       = { [ordered]@{ Mac = $_.general.name; FileVault = $_.operatingSystem.fileVault2Status; macOS = $_.operatingSystem.version; 'Last contact' = $_.general.lastContact } }
        MinimumPercent = $MinimumPercent
        Requirement    = 'have FileVault on'
        NoDeviceReason = 'Jamf Pro manages no Mac that reports its FileVault status.'
    }
    Measure-JamfDevice @measure
}

input.content:
FileVault encrypts a Mac's startup disk, so the data on a lost or stolen Mac cannot be read without the user's
password or the recovery key. This test counts the Macs that Jamf Pro manages whose startup disk is encrypted, from
the FileVault status each Mac reports in its inventory. Macs that cannot report a status are left out.

It reports on rule `system_settings_filevault_enforce` of the NIST macOS Security Compliance Project, which the CIS
macOS benchmarks and the DISA macOS STIG also require.

#### Remediation action

1. In Jamf Pro, go to **Computers** > **Configuration Profiles** and open (or create) the profile that manages
   FileVault.
2. Add the **Security & Privacy** > **FileVault** payload (or **FileVault** in Jamf Pro 11), turn on **Require
   FileVault**, and escrow the personal recovery key to Jamf Pro.
3. Scope the profile to all managed computers, and check **Computers** > **Inventory** for Macs still not encrypted.
4. Raise or lower the share this test needs with the `MinimumPercent` parameter.

- [Jamf Pro documentation: Managing FileVault](https://learn.jamf.com/r/en-US/jamf-pro-documentation-current/Administering_FileVault_on_macOS_10.14_or_Later)

Rules:
- Each check is tests/Test.MP.JAMF.<n>.ps1 (one function Test-MPJAMF<n> with a [MaesterTest(...)] attribute) plus tests/Test.MP.JAMF.<n>.md. Attribute: Id, Title (plain sentence stating the good state, no "(Preview)"), Product = 'Jamf Pro', Feature (short title-case free text, reuse the same Feature names across checks: 'Single sign-on', 'Administrator accounts', 'API clients', 'Server', 'Enrollment', 'Automated Device Enrollment', 'Webhooks', 'Disk encryption', 'Mac security', 'macOS updates', 'Inventory', 'Mobile device security', 'Compliance benchmarks'), Area and ResourceType from the taxonomy keys, Severity, UserImpact, ImplementationCost (rubric), Mitre (valid IDs, techniques the control prevents or detects), Control (first the requirement of a framework file the pack ships when one applies: 'disa-jamf-pro-stig:V-xxxxxx' or 'mscp:<rule id>' — the ID must exist in tests/frameworks/*.json; then 'nist-800-53-r5:<control>'), Service = 'JAMF.JamfPro' (or 'JAMF.Platform' for the Compliance Benchmarks family), Author = 'merill'.

Never call Invoke-RestMethod/Invoke-WebRequest. Results go through Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result (Markdown; use ConvertTo-JamfMarkdownTable for lists). Fleet shares use Measure-JamfDevice. You may add a helper in helpers/ (one function per file, Verb-Noun name with a Jamf prefix, comment-based help) when two or more checks need it; never edit helpers another group may use without keeping their behaviour.
- Pack files may hold only functions. Do not invoke script blocks with & or call a command whose name is computed (the pack's security scan flags it as DynamicCode): pass script blocks to Where-Object -FilterScript or ForEach-Object -Process instead.
- No connection checks and no outer try/catch in a check: the engine gates on Service and turns errors into Error rows. Use Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause NotApplicable (or Custom with -SkippedCustomReason) for conditions only the check can see (for example SSO turned off for a check that only applies with SSO). Use -Investigate when a person must judge the result.
- Parameters: thresholds with ValidateRange and a one-line # comment above each; string[] lists for exceptions (names of accounts or API clients). Defaults must make sense for most organisations.
- The .md: what the check looks at and why it matters (2 short paragraphs, plain direct sentences, no em-dash asides, no marketing words), the framework requirement it supports, then '#### Remediation action' with numbered steps naming the Jamf Pro UI path (Settings > ...), then '#### Related links' (learn.jamf.com pages you are confident exist, or developer.jamf.com), then a line '<!--- Results --->' and '%TestResult%'. Other groups write files at the same time; if their spec fails, ignore it but make sure yours passes.
- Return a short report: the checks you wrote (ID, title, endpoint, pass rule, parameters, Control), helpers added, anything you could not verify.`

**Still uncertain**
- **Exemplar 1018 breaks the rubric.** It repeats `nist-800-53-r5:SC-28`, which is already in the `Related` list of `system_settings_filevault_enforce`. It isn't one of this group's files, so I left it.
- **Menu paths still from memory:** the SIP criterion in Search Inventory, the "Jailbreak Detected" smart group criterion, the "Issue New Recovery Key" policy action, the "Last Check-in" criterion, and **Settings** > **Computer management** > **Check-In**.
- **Area of 1024 (check-in) is a judgement call.** It is `devices`. The rubric sends inventory and health tests to `infrastructure`, but stale managed devices are mainly a device management concern.
- **1019 Severity Medium and 1021 Severity High are defensible but arguable.** 1019 is about keeping data recoverable rather than stopping an attacker, which could argue for Low. 1021 checks the main control against users opening malicious downloads, which supports High, but users can override Gatekeeper per app.
- **Version defaults:** 1023's default of macOS 15 and 1028's default of 26 assume macOS 27 and iOS 27 have shipped. Users will need to raise them over time.
- **Real tenant:** nothing has been run against a live Jamf Pro server, only the recorded answers in the spec.

1	function Get-JamfComplianceBenchmarkRule {
2	    <#
3	    .SYNOPSIS
4	    Returns one instance per rule of every Jamf Compliance Benchmark, with the rule's results across its devices.
5	
6	    .DESCRIPTION
7	    Reads GET /compliance-benchmarks/v1/benchmarks and, for each benchmark, every page of
8	    GET /compliance-benchmarks/v1/benchmarks/{id}/rules through the Jamf Platform API. Rule IDs are mSCP rule IDs;
9	    a rule that the pack's mSCP framework file knows is mapped to it. When there is no benchmark, returns one
10	    instance that the test skips with how to create one.
11	    #>
12	    [CmdletBinding()]
13	    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
14	    param()
15	
16	    $benchmarks = @((Invoke-JamfPlatformRequest -Path 'compliance-benchmarks/v1/benchmarks').benchmarks | Where-Object { $_ -and [string]$_.syncState -ne 'DELETING' })
17	    if ($benchmarks.Count -eq 0) {
18	        return [pscustomobject]@{ Id = 'no-benchmarks'; Title = 'Jamf Compliance Benchmarks has no benchmark'; Data = $null }
19	    }
20	
21	    # The mSCP rules the pack's framework file knows, so an instance can name its requirement.
22	    $framework = Join-Path -Path $PSScriptRoot -ChildPath 'frameworks/mscp.json'
23	    $known = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([System.StringComparer]::Ordinal)
24	    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $framework) {
25	        foreach ($id in (Get-Content -LiteralPath $framework -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json).Requirements.Id) { $null = $known.Add([string]$id) }
26	    }
27	
28	    $slugs = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([System.StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)
29	    foreach ($benchmark in $benchmarks) {
30	        $title = [string]$benchmark.title
31	        $base = ($title.ToLowerInvariant() -replace '[^a-z0-9]+', '-').Trim('-')
32	        if ($base.Length -gt 40) { $base = $base.Substring(0, 40).Trim('-') }
33	        if (-not $base) { $base = 'benchmark' }
34	        # Two benchmarks with the same title still get IDs of their own.
35	        $slug = $base
36	        $n = 2
37	        while (-not $slugs.Add($slug)) { $slug = "$base-$n"; $n++ }
38	
39	        $rules = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()
40	        $page = 0
41	        do {
42	            $response = Invoke-JamfPlatformRequest -Path "compliance-benchmarks/v1/benchmarks/$([uri]::EscapeDataString([string]$benchmark.id))/rules?page=$page&page-size=500"
43	            foreach ($rule in @($response.results)) { if ($null -ne $rule) { $rules.Add($rule) } }
44	            $page++
45	        } while (@($response.results).Count -gt 0 -and $rules.Count -lt [int]$response.totalCount)
46	
47	        $seen = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([System.StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)
48	        foreach ($rule in $rules) {
49	            $ruleId = [string]$rule.ruleId
50	            $suffix = "$slug.$($ruleId -replace '[^A-Za-z0-9._-]', '-')"
51	            if ($suffix.Length -gt 128) { $suffix = $suffix.Substring(0, 128) }
52	            if (-not $seen.Add($suffix)) { continue }
53	
54	            $ruleTitle = if ($rule.ruleNumber) { "$($rule.ruleNumber) $($rule.ruleTitle)" } else { [string]$rule.ruleTitle }
55	            $instance = [ordered]@{
56	                Id     = $suffix
57	                Title  = $ruleTitle
58	                Fields = @{ Benchmark = $title; Section = [string]$rule.sectionName }
59	                Data   = $rule
60	            }
61	            if ($known.Contains($ruleId)) { $instance.Control = "mscp:$ruleId" }
62	            [pscustomobject]$instance
63	        }
64	    }
65	}

# Jamf Pro pack for Maester

A [Maester Pack](https://maester.dev/docs/next/packs) that checks the security of a Jamf Pro server and of the
Macs, iPhones and iPads it manages. It reads Jamf Pro through its API and never changes anything.

- **The server:** single sign-on, administrator accounts, API clients, version, sign-in notice, enrollment and
  webhooks. Checks name the rule of the [DISA Jamf Pro v10.x EMM STIG](https://public.cyber.mil/stigs/downloads/)
  (V3R2, 30 Sep 2026) they support.
- **The fleet:** FileVault and recovery keys, System Integrity Protection, Gatekeeper, the firewall, macOS
  versions, check-in, passcodes, jailbreaks and iOS versions, from Jamf Pro's inventory. Mac checks name their rule
  of the [NIST macOS Security Compliance Project](https://github.com/usnistgov/macos_security) (mSCP, release
  27.1), which brings the CIS macOS benchmark, DISA macOS STIG, NIST SP 800-53 and CMMC references with it.
- **Compliance Benchmarks:** when you connect the Jamf Platform API too, each rule of your Jamf Compliance
  Benchmarks is a result of its own, mapped to its mSCP rule.

It needs Maester 3.0 or later and Jamf Pro 10.49 or later, on Jamf Cloud or your own server.

## Checks

| ID | Check | Severity | Framework rule |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MP.JAMF.1001 | Jamf Pro administrators sign in with single sign-on | High | STIG V-241796 |
| MP.JAMF.1002 | Users cannot bypass single sign-on | Medium | STIG V-241797 |
| MP.JAMF.1003 | Jamf Pro reaches the SAML identity provider over HTTPS | Medium | STIG V-241818 |
| MP.JAMF.1004 | Few accounts have full administrator access | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1005 | Only break-glass accounts sign in with a Jamf Pro password | Medium | STIG V-241817 |
| MP.JAMF.1006 | Local account passwords are changed within 180 days | Low | STIG V-241810 |
| MP.JAMF.1007 | No API client can read device secrets | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1008 | API clients that can change Jamf Pro are reviewed | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1009 | API client access tokens are short-lived | Low | |
| MP.JAMF.1010 | Jamf Pro runs a supported version | High | STIG V-241798 |
| MP.JAMF.1011 | The Jamf Pro sign-in page shows a use notice | Low | STIG V-241794 |
| MP.JAMF.1012 | User-initiated enrollment of Macs is off or limited to reviewed groups | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1013 | Computer PreStage enrollments keep the MDM profile on Macs | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1014 | Computer PreStage enrollments require the user to sign in | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1015 | Mobile device PreStage enrollments supervise devices and keep the MDM profile | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1016 | Automated Device Enrollment tokens are not about to expire | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1017 | Webhooks send over HTTPS with authentication | Low | |
| MP.JAMF.1018 | FileVault encrypts managed Macs | High | mSCP system_settings_filevault_enforce |
| MP.JAMF.1019 | FileVault recovery keys of encrypted Macs are escrowed and valid | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1020 | System Integrity Protection is on for managed Macs | Medium | mSCP os_sip_enable |
| MP.JAMF.1021 | Gatekeeper is on for managed Macs | High | mSCP os_gatekeeper_enable |
| MP.JAMF.1022 | The macOS firewall is on for managed Macs | Medium | mSCP system_settings_firewall_enable |
| MP.JAMF.1023 | Managed Macs run a supported macOS version | High | |
| MP.JAMF.1024 | Managed Macs check in with Jamf Pro | Low | |
| MP.JAMF.1025 | Macs pass the mSCP compliance script | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1026 | Managed mobile devices have a passcode that meets the profile | High | |
| MP.JAMF.1027 | No managed mobile device is jailbroken | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1028 | Managed iPhones and iPads run a supported iOS or iPadOS version | High | |
| MP.JAMF.2001 | Devices pass the rules of Jamf Compliance Benchmarks (one result per rule) | Medium | mSCP rule of each result |

Checks without a framework rule still name the NIST SP 800-53 controls they support. Most of the STIG is about the
server's operating system, database and firewall, or the console's password policy, which Jamf Pro's API does not
expose; the pack checks the 8 rules the API can show.

## Connect

### Jamf Pro

1. In Jamf Pro, go to **Settings** > **System** > **API roles and clients**.
2. On **API Roles**, create a role named `Maester (read only)` with these privileges:

   | Privilege | Used by |
   | --- | --- |
   | Read SSO Settings | 1001, 1002, 1003, 1005 |
   | Read Accounts | 1004, 1005, 1006 |
   | Read Account Groups | 1004 |
   | Read API Roles | 1007, 1008 |
   | Read API Integrations | 1007, 1008, 1009 |
   | Read User-Initiated Enrollment | 1012 |
   | Read Computer PreStage Enrollments | 1013, 1014 |
   | Read Mobile Device PreStage Enrollments | 1015 |
   | Read Device Enrollment Program Instances | 1016 |
   | Read Webhooks | 1017 |
   | Read Computers | 1018 to 1025 |
   | Read Mobile Devices | 1026 to 1028 |

   The version, cloud information and sign-in notice (1010, 1011) need no privilege. Never give the role a
   Create, Update, Delete or View privilege: the pack does not need one. A check whose privilege is missing
   reports an Error that names the API path it could not read.
3. On **API Clients**, create a client with that role, enable it, and generate a client secret. Note the client ID
   and secret.
4. Connect Maester. Keep the secret in an environment variable rather than in a file:

```powershell
Install-MtPack maester365/maester-pack-jamf
$env:MAESTER_JAMF_JAMFPRO_CLIENTSECRET = 'REDACTED'
Connect-Maester -Service JAMF.JamfPro -ServiceSetting @{ Server = 'https://contoso.jamfcloud.com'; ClientId = '<client id>' }
Invoke-Maester -Pack JAMF -SkipBuiltIn
```

The server can also be your own, such as `jamf.contoso.com:8443`. A Jamf Pro account works instead of an API
client (`Username` and `Password`), but API clients are the better choice: they have only the privileges you give
them and need no person's password.

### Jamf Compliance Benchmarks (optional)

MP.JAMF.2001 reads the results of [Compliance Benchmarks](https://learn.jamf.com/r/en-US/jamf-compliance-benchmarks-configuration-guide/Compliance_Benchmarks_Requirements)
through the Jamf Platform API. It needs Jamf Cloud and Jamf Pro 11.16 or later, and its own credentials:

1. In [Jamf Account](https://account.jamf.com), create an integration scoped to your Jamf Pro environment with only
   the `compliance-benchmarks:read` scope. Note the client ID, the secret and the environment ID shown in the
   integration's details. Integrations are valid for six months.
2. Connect:

```powershell
$env:MAESTER_JAMF_PLATFORM_CLIENTSECRET = 'REDACTED'
Connect-Maester -Service JAMF.Platform -ServiceSetting @{ Region = 'us'; ClientId = '<client id>'; EnvironmentId = '<environment id>' }
```

`Region` is `us`, `eu` or `apac`. MP.JAMF.2001 does not run until JAMF.Platform is connected.

## Run it in a pipeline

The pack signs in with a client secret, so it runs unattended. Set the connection in environment variables, which
`Connect-Maester` reads (`MAESTER_JAMF_JAMFPRO_<SETTING>` and `MAESTER_JAMF_PLATFORM_<SETTING>`):

```powershell
$env:MAESTER_JAMF_JAMFPRO_SERVER = 'https://contoso.jamfcloud.com'
$env:MAESTER_JAMF_JAMFPRO_CLIENTID = '<client id>'
$env:MAESTER_JAMF_JAMFPRO_CLIENTSECRET = 'REDACTED'
Connect-Maester -Service JAMF.JamfPro
Invoke-Maester -Pack JAMF -SkipBuiltIn -NonInteractive
```

Settings that are not secrets can go in `maester-config.json` instead:

```json
{ "Connections": { "JAMF.JamfPro": { "Server": "https://contoso.jamfcloud.com", "ClientId": "<client id>" } } }
```

## Settings

Thresholds and exceptions are test parameters. Set them per test under `TestSettings` in `maester-config.json`:

```json
{
  "TestSettings": [
    { "Id": "MP.JAMF.1005", "Parameters": { "BreakGlassAccounts": ["jamf-breakglass"] } },
    { "Id": "MP.JAMF.1018", "Parameters": { "MinimumPercent": 98 } }
  ]
}
```

| Check | Parameter | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MP.JAMF.1004 | MaximumAdministrators | 5 | Highest number of people with full administrator access |
| MP.JAMF.1005 | BreakGlassAccounts | none | Break-glass accounts that keep a Jamf Pro password; not counted |
| MP.JAMF.1005 | MaximumLocalAccounts | 2 | Highest number of other enabled local accounts |
| MP.JAMF.1006 | BreakGlassAccounts | none | Break-glass accounts whose password is not checked |
| MP.JAMF.1006 | MaximumPasswordAgeDays | 180 | Oldest a local account's password may be, in days |
| MP.JAMF.1007 | AllowedApiClients | none | API clients (name or client ID) allowed to read device secrets |
| MP.JAMF.1008 | AllowedApiClients | none | API clients reviewed and allowed to keep write privileges |
| MP.JAMF.1009 | MaximumTokenLifetimeSeconds | 1800 | Longest access token lifetime |
| MP.JAMF.1010 | MinimumVersion | 11.30.0 | Oldest Jamf Pro version accepted on a server you host |
| MP.JAMF.1016 | WarningDays | 30 | Days before a token expires that the check starts to fail |
| MP.JAMF.1017 | ExcludedWebhook | none | Webhooks that may send without HTTPS or authentication |
| MP.JAMF.1018 to 1027 | MinimumPercent | 95 or 100 | Lowest share of devices that must meet the check |
| MP.JAMF.1023 | MinimumMajorVersion | 15 | Oldest major macOS version that counts as supported |
| MP.JAMF.1024 | MaximumDaysSinceContact | 30 | Days without contact before a Mac counts as not checking in |
| MP.JAMF.1028 | MinimumMajorVersion | 26 | Oldest major iOS or iPadOS version that counts as supported |
| MP.JAMF.2001 | MinimumPassPercent | 100 | Lowest share of devices that must pass a benchmark rule when some fail |

Raise `MinimumVersion` and the two `MinimumMajorVersion` values as Jamf and Apple release new versions.

## How results map

Each check names its framework requirement in `Control`, and Maester adds the requirement's facts to the result's
`Benchmark`, so the report's framework view shows the pack's results under each rule:

- `disa-jamf-pro-stig:<Vuln ID>`, with the rule's STIG ID, rule ID, severity (CAT I to III) and CCIs, from
  [tests/frameworks/disa-jamf-pro-stig.json](tests/frameworks/disa-jamf-pro-stig.json).
- `mscp:<rule ID>`, with the mSCP baselines that include the rule and its CIS macOS, DISA macOS STIG, NIST SP
  800-53, NIST SP 800-171, CMMC and CIS Controls references, from
  [tests/frameworks/mscp.json](tests/frameworks/mscp.json).

The framework files hold identifiers and facts only, never the text of a rule.

## Maintaining the pack

Regenerate the framework files when a new release comes out:

```powershell
# mSCP: clone the release tag, then generate (needs the powershell-yaml module)
git clone --depth 1 --branch release_27.1 https://github.com/usnistgov/macos_security ../macos_security
./build/Update-MscpFramework.ps1 -MscpPath ../macos_security -MacOSVersion 27

# DISA Jamf Pro STIG: download and unzip it from https://public.cyber.mil/stigs/downloads/
./build/Update-JamfStigFramework.ps1 -XccdfPath ./REDACTED.xml
```

Then update the framework `Version` in [tests/suite.json](tests/suite.json).

The pack's tests in [spec/](spec/) run every check against recorded Jamf API answers, with no Jamf server:

```powershell
Invoke-Pester ./spec
```

Set `MAESTER_MODULE` to a `Maester.psd1` to test against a checkout of Maester. The pack check
([check-pack.yml](.github/workflows/check-pack.yml)) runs them on Ubuntu and Windows, and runs `Test-MtPack` on the
files the pack ships.

### Versions and releases

Releases work as in the [demo pack](https://github.com/maester365/maester-pack-demo#versions-and-releases): with
the repository variable `PACK_RELEASES` set to `true`, every merged pull request gets the next version and a
release, with its notes from [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). Without it, `Install-MtPack` installs `main`.

## Files

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `maester-pack.json` | The manifest: ID, code, connectors, suite and helpers |
| `maester-pack.guide.json` | How to install, connect and run the pack, for its page on the pack index |
| `connector/` | The JAMF.JamfPro and JAMF.Platform connectors: sign-in, token renewal and sign-out |
| `helpers/` | The one function that sends requests, cached reads of the APIs, and shared result formatting |
| `tests/` | The checks and their guides, `suite.json`, and the framework files in `tests/frameworks/` |
| `build/` | Generators of the framework files (not shipped) |
| `spec/` | The pack's Pester tests and their recorded Jamf answers (not shipped) |

## Security

The pack only reads. Every request goes through one function, [Invoke-JamfHttp](helpers/Invoke-JamfHttp.ps1),
which sends HTTPS only and refuses any POST except the requests that get or end a token. Because each customer's
Jamf server has its own address, the request address is built at run time, which the Maester Packs scan rates
Medium risk. Tokens and secrets stay in the PowerShell session and are never written to the report. See
[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) to report a problem.

## Licence

The pack is [MIT](LICENSE) licensed.

`tests/frameworks/mscp.json` is derived from the [NIST macOS Security Compliance Project](https://github.com/usnistgov/macos_security),
which is licensed [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) and includes contributions from the
US Government, the public and Apple Inc. Only rule identifiers and references are used; no Apple vendor
description text is included.

`tests/frameworks/disa-jamf-pro-stig.json` lists identifiers from the DISA Jamf Pro v10.x EMM STIG, a work of the
US Government in the public domain.

| MP.JAMF.1010 | MinimumVersion | 11.30.0 | Oldest Jamf Pro version accepted on a server you host |
| MP.JAMF.1016 | WarningDays | 30 | Days before a token expires that the check starts to fail |
| MP.JAMF.1017 | ExcludedWebhook | none | Webhooks that may send without HTTPS or authentication |
| MP.JAMF.1018 to 1027 | MinimumPercent | 90 to 100 | Lowest share of devices that must meet the check |
| MP.JAMF.1023 | MinimumMajorVersion | 15 | Oldest major macOS version that counts as supported |
| MP.JAMF.1024 | MaximumDaysSinceContact | 30 | Days without contact before a Mac counts as not checking in |
| MP.JAMF.1028 | MinimumMajorVersion | 26 | Oldest major iOS or iPadOS version that counts as supported |
| MP.JAMF.2001 | MinimumPassPercent | 100 | Lowest share of devices that must pass a benchmark rule when some fail |

Raise `MinimumVersion` and the two `MinimumMajorVersion` values as Jamf and Apple release new versions.

## How results map

Each check names its framework requirement in `Control`, and Maester adds the requirement's facts to the result's
`Benchmark`, so the report's framework view shows the pack's results under each rule:

- `disa-jamf-pro-stig:<Vuln ID>`, with the rule's STIG ID, rule ID, severity (CAT I to III) and CCIs, from
  [tests/frameworks/disa-jamf-pro-stig.json](tests/frameworks/disa-jamf-pro-stig.json).
- `mscp:<rule ID>`, with the mSCP baselines that include the rule and its CIS macOS, DISA macOS STIG, NIST SP
  800-53, NIST SP 800-171, CMMC and CIS Controls references, from
  [tests/frameworks/mscp.json](tests/frameworks/mscp.json).

The framework files hold identifiers and facts only, never the text of a rule.

## Maintaining the pack

Regenerate the framework files when a new release comes out:

```powershell
# mSCP: clone the release tag, then generate (needs the powershell-yaml module)
git clone --depth 1 --branch release_27.1 https://github.com/usnistgov/macos_security ../macos_security
./build/Update-MscpFramework.ps1 -MscpPath ../macos_security -MacOSVersion 27

# DISA Jamf Pro STIG: download and unzip it from https://public.cyber.mil/stigs/downloads/
./build/Update-JamfStigFramework.ps1 -XccdfPath ./REDACTED.xml
```

Then update the framework `Version` in [tests/suite.json](tests/suite.json).

The pack's tests in [spec/](spec/) run every check against recorded Jamf API answers, with no Jamf server:

```powershell
Invoke-Pester ./spec
```

Set `MAESTER_MODULE` to a `Maester.psd1` to test against a checkout of Maester. The pack check
([check-pack.yml](.github/workflows/check-pack.yml)) runs them on Ubuntu and Windows, and runs `Test-MtPack` on the
files the pack ships.

### Versions and releases

Releases work as in the [demo pack](https://github.com/maester365/maester-pack-demo#versions-and-releases): with
the repository variable `PACK_RELEASES` set to `true`, every merged pull request gets the next version and a
release, with its notes from [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). Without it, `Install-MtPack` installs `main`.

## Files

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `maester-pack.json` | The manifest: ID, code, connectors, suite and helpers |
| `maester-pack.guide.json` | How to install, connect and run the pack, for its page on the pack index |
| `connector/` | The JAMF.JamfPro and JAMF.Platform connectors: sign-in, token renewal and sign-out |
| `helpers/` | The one function that sends requests, cached reads of the APIs, and shared result formatting |
| `tests/` | The checks and their guides, `suite.json`, and the framework files in `tests/frameworks/` |
| `build/` | Generators of the framework files (not shipped) |
| `spec/` | The pack's Pester tests (not shipped) |

## Security

The pack only reads. Every request goes through one function, [Invoke-JamfHttp](helpers/Invoke-JamfHttp.ps1),
which sends HTTPS only and refuses any POST except the requests that get or end a token. Because each customer's
Jamf server has its own address, the request address is built at run time, which the Maester Packs scan rates
Medium risk. Tokens and secrets stay in the PowerShell session and are never written to the report. See
[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) to report a problem.

## Licence

The pack is [MIT](LICENSE) licensed.

`tests/frameworks/mscp.json` is derived from the [NIST macOS Security Compliance Project](https://github.com/usnistgov/macos_security),
which is licensed [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) and includes contributions from the
US Government, the public and Apple Inc. Only rule identifiers and references are used; no Apple vendor
description text is included.

`tests/frameworks/disa-jamf-pro-stig.json` lists identifiers from the DISA Jamf Pro v10.x EMM STIG, a work of the
US Government in the public domain.
EOF
cd ~/github/maester-pack-jamf; cat > SECURITY.md <<'EOF'
# Security

Report a security problem in this pack privately, through
[GitHub's private vulnerability reporting](https://github.com/maester365/maester-pack-jamf/security/advisories/new),
not in a public issue. The same link is the pack's `SecurityContact` in `maester-pack.json`.

A problem in Maester itself goes to [maester365/maester](https://github.com/maester365/maester/security).
EOF
cat > CHANGELOG.md <<'EOF'
# Changelog

Every release of the pack, newest first. Install-MtPack shows the version; Update-MtPack moves to a newer one.

## 0.1.0

- The first release: 28 checks of the Jamf Pro server (single sign-on, administrator accounts, API clients,
  version, sign-in notice, enrollment, webhooks) and of the Macs, iPhones and iPads it manages (FileVault and
  recovery keys, System Integrity Protection, Gatekeeper, firewall, OS versions, check-in, mSCP compliance script
  results, passcodes, jailbreaks), and one result per rule of Jamf Compliance Benchmarks through the Jamf Platform
  API. Checks name the DISA Jamf Pro v10.x EMM STIG (V3R2) and NIST macOS Security Compliance Project (release
  27.1) rules they support.
EOF
