I've built the Jamf Pro pack in `~/github/maester-pack-jamf`, set up like the ScubaGear and ScubaGoggles packs. All 126 spec cases pass against recorded Jamf API answers, and the shipped files pass `Test-MtPack -Official` at Medium risk. Nothing has run against a real Jamf server yet, and nothing is committed or pushed.

**What's in it**
- **Two connectors:**
  - **`JAMF.JamfPro`** signs in with a Jamf Pro API client or account and gets a new token before the old one expires.
  - **`JAMF.Platform`** is for Compliance Benchmarks. It needs a separate Jamf Account integration and only runs once you connect it.
- **28 checks plus one family:**
  - **Server:** single sign-on, SSO bypass, the identity provider over HTTPS, the number of full administrators, local break-glass accounts and their password age, API clients that can read device secrets or change Jamf Pro, token lifetime, version, sign-in notice.
  - **Enrollment and webhooks:** user-initiated enrollment, PreStage enrollments (MDM profile removable, sign-in required, supervision), enrollment token expiry, webhook HTTPS and authentication.
  - **Fleet:** FileVault and recovery-key escrow, System Integrity Protection, Gatekeeper, firewall, macOS and iOS versions, check-in, passcodes, jailbreaks, and results of the mSCP compliance script.
  - **MP.JAMF.2001:** one result per rule of your Jamf Compliance Benchmarks, each mapped to its mSCP rule.
- **Framework files**, generated by scripts in `build/`:
  - the DISA Jamf Pro STIG (V3R2, 29 rules)
  - mSCP release 27.1 (352 macOS rules), which carries the CIS macOS, DISA macOS STIG, NIST 800-53/171 and CMMC references
- **Repo files:** README (API role privileges, connect, settings), pack guide, CI workflows and a Pester spec that runs every check with no Jamf server.

**Limits you should know about**
- **The STIG mostly can't be checked remotely.** The API can show only about 8 of the 29 rules. The rest cover the server's operating system, database, firewall, or the console password policy, which has no API.
- **Some field meanings are inferred from their names.** Examples: `ssoBypassAllowed` as the "allow users to bypass SSO" option, and a local account read from its account type. The Classic API privilege name "Read Webhooks" is also unconfirmed. A run on a real server will settle these.
- **Version defaults will go stale.** The minimums are Jamf Pro 11.30.0, macOS 15 and iOS 26. They are parameters, so users can raise them.
- **MP.JAMF.2001 is untested against the live API.** Compliance Benchmarks only works on Jamf Cloud and its API is still labelled Beta.
- **Test code:** JAMF wasn't claimed on packs.maester.cloud when I checked.

Before any release, someone needs to run it against a Jamf Pro tenant, as you planned for ScubaGear.
Commit and create repo

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Maester 3.0 packs.** A pack has:
     - `maester-pack.json` (Id, Guid, Code, Suites, Helpers, Connectors, Uses);
     - native tests `Test.MP.<Code>.<n>.ps1` with a `[MaesterTest]` attribute, plus a `.md` guide;
     - `suite.json`, which declares `Frameworks`, and the framework files `tests/frameworks/<key>.json`.
   - **Families.** `InstanceSource` makes a test a family; each instance has an Id matching `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$`, and can set Control and Fields.
   - **Connections.**
     - `Set-MtConnectionState`, `Get-MtConnectionState` and `Clear-MtConnectionState` need `-Service` when a pack has two connectors.
     - `ExpiresOn` in the state makes Maester call Renew within 10 minutes of expiry.
     - Connector settings come from `-ServiceSetting`, `MAESTER_<SERVICE>_<PARAM>` environment variables, or `Connections.<Service>` in the config. Only `Connect-Maester` reads them.
     - `"OptIn": true` means a test does not run while its service is not connected.
   - **Pack scan (Test-MtPackContent).**
     - Files may hold only functions.
     - Calling a script block with `&`, or a computed command name, is a Medium DynamicCode finding.
     - A request URL built at run time is a Medium DynamicUrl finding.
     - The publisher `maester365` needs `-Official`.
     - `build/` and `spec/` are export-ignored, so the check runs on a git archive.
   - **Add-MtTestResultDetail.** Uses `-Result`, `-Investigate`, and `-SkippedBecause NotApplicable|Custom -SkippedCustomReason`.
   - **Jamf Pro API.**
     - Token: `POST /api/v1/oauth/token` (client credentials; returns access_token and expires_in). Accounts use `POST /api/v1/auth/token` with basic auth.
     - Sign-out: `POST /api/v1/auth/invalidate-token`.
     - Endpoints: `/api/v3/sso`, `/api/v1/accounts`, `/api/v1/account-groups`, `/api/v1/api-roles`, `/api/v1/api-integrations`, `/api/v1/jamf-pro-version`, `/api/v1/cloud-information`, `/api/v1/login-customization`, `/api/v4/enrollment`, `/api/v3/enrollment/access-groups`, `/api/v3/computer-prestages`, `/api/v3/mobile-device-prestages`, `/api/v1/device-enrollments`, Classic `JSSResource/webhooks`, `/api/v4/computers-inventory` (falls back to v3), `/api/v2/mobile-devices/detail`.
     - There is no password-policy API.
   - **Jamf Platform API.**
     - Host and token: `https://{region}.api.jamfcloud.com`, token at `/auth/token` (15 minutes).
     - Every request needs the `X-Environment-Id` header.
     - Endpoints: `compliance-benchmarks/v1/benchmarks` and `/v1/benchmarks/{id}/rules`.
     - Rule IDs are mSCP rule IDs.
     - Credentials come from a Jamf Account integration with `compliance-benchmarks:read`.
   - **Standards and licences.**
     - mSCP release 27.1 (CC BY 4.0) uses the 2.0 layout: `src/mscp/data/rules`, with `rules` a symlink. Use `find -L`.
     - The DISA Jamf Pro STIG V3R2 (30 Sep 2026, 29 rules) is public domain XCCDF.

   - **Helpers (one function per file):**
     - `Invoke-JamfHttp` is the only Invoke-RestMethod call. It sends HTTPS only, allows POST only with `-TokenRequest`, and retries 429/503.

     - `Update-JamfProToken` and `Update-JamfPlatformToken` get tokens.

content.text:
I created the private repo at https://github.com/maester365/maester-pack-jamf, pushed `main` with the commit `dbbf1d3`, and added the description, homepage and topics.

- **CI:** [Check pack](https://github.com/maester365/maester-pack-jamf/actions/runs/42551824868) passed on Linux and Windows. That run covers the spec tests and the pack content checks on the shipped archive. The only warnings are GitHub notices about the Node 20 deprecation in `actions/checkout@v4` and the Ubuntu runner migration.
- **Release:** the workflow skipped, as it should, because the version hasn't been bumped. Nothing is published.
- **Branch protection:** not applied yet. The ruleset is in `.github/rulesets/main.json` but GitHub doesn't apply it automatically, so you'll need to import it under Settings → Rules.

Before you make the repo public, run the pack against a real Jamf Pro tenant. That run will settle a few field meanings I inferred from their names (such as `ssoBypassAllowed`), the Classic privilege name "Read Webhooks", and whether the Compliance Benchmarks results come back as expected.
